Lesson / Topic: Defining relative clauses: Who, which, that, where
Core idea: Defining relative clause patikslina, apie kurį konkretų žmogų ar daiktą kalbame.
Main rule / explanation: Who – žmonėms. Which/that – daiktams įprastose defining clauses. Where – vietoms.
Form / structure: person + who + clause. thing + which/that + clause. place + where + clause.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai reikia patikslinti, apie kurį konkretų žmogų, daiktą ar vietą kalbame.
Examples:
The girl who won the race is my friend. → Mergaitė, kuri laimėjo lenktynes, yra mano draugė.
The dog that I saw was very big. → Šuo, kurį mačiau, buvo labai didelis.
This is the park where we play. → Tai parkas, kuriame žaidžiame.
The book that you gave me is funny. → Knyga, kurią man davei, yra juokinga.
Special cases / exceptions: Nedėk antro subject po who/which/that, jei santykinis žodis jau yra reikiama sakinio dalis.
Common mistakes:
❌ The analyst who she prepared the report... → ✅ The analyst who prepared the report...
❌ The file that you sent it... → ✅ The file that you sent...
Don't confuse with: Relative clause atsako į klausimą „kuris būtent žmogus / daiktas / vieta?“
Quick summary / memory hook:
who → žmonės.
which/that → daiktai.
where → vietos.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: So, neither: so am I, neither do I, etc.
Core idea: So ir neither leidžia trumpai parodyti, kad sutinkame su kito žmogaus teiginiu arba neiginiu.
Main rule / explanation: Positive agreement: So + auxiliary + subject. Negative agreement: Neither + auxiliary + subject. Pagalbinis veiksmažodis turi atitikti pirmąją frazę.
Form / structure: So am I. / So do I. / So can I. / So have I. Neither do I. / Neither have I.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai norime trumpai pasakyti „aš taip pat“ arba „aš irgi ne“, vartodami tą patį pagalbinį veiksmažodį.
Examples:
'I am happy.' — 'So am I.' → „Aš laimingas.“ — „Aš taip pat.“
'I like pizza.' — 'So do I.' → „Man patinka pica.“ — „Man irgi.“
'I don't play chess.' — 'Neither do I.' → „Aš nežaidžiu šachmatais.“ — „Aš irgi ne.“
'She can swim.' — 'So can I.' → „Ji moka plaukti.“ — „Aš irgi.
Special cases / exceptions: Nenaudok do automatiškai. Žiūrėk į originalų sakinį: be, do, have arba modal.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am tired. — So do I. → ✅ So am I.
❌ He hasn't finished. — Neither do I. → ✅ Neither have I.
Don't confuse with: Tai nėra naujas laikas. Tai trumpa agreement struktūra.
Quick summary / memory hook:
So = positive agreement.
Neither = negative agreement.
Auxiliary must match.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Auxiliary verbs: do, be and have
Core idea: Auxiliary verbs do, be ir have padeda kurti gramatines konstrukcijas. Kartais jie neperduoda pagrindinės reikšmės, o rodo klausimą, neiginį arba laiką.
Main rule / explanation: Do/does/did padeda sudaryti klausimus ir neiginius su įprastais veiksmažodžiais. Be sudaro Continuous ir Passive. Have/has/had sudaro Perfect.
Form / structure: Do: Do you work? / She doesn't work. Be: is working / was checked. Have: have finished / had left.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai reikia suprasti do, be ir have vaidmenį klausimuose, neiginiuose, Continuous, Passive ir Perfect konstrukcijose.
Examples:
Do you like cats? → Ar tau patinka katės?
She is reading. → Ji dabar skaito.
They have finished the game. → Jie baigė žaidimą.
He doesn't play tennis. → Jis nežaidžia teniso.
We have seen this film. → Mes matėme šį filmą.
Special cases / exceptions: Pagalbinis veiksmažodis yra gramatinės konstrukcijos dalis. Jo nereikia kiekvieną kartą versti atskiru žodžiu.
Common mistakes:
❌ She does working. → ✅ She is working.
❌ Did you worked? → ✅ Did you work?
❌ They have finish. → ✅ They have finished.
Don't confuse with: Do = questions/negatives su ordinary verbs. Be = continuous/passive. Have = perfect.
Quick summary / memory hook:
do → questions/negatives.
be → continuous/passive.
have → perfect.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs
Core idea: Comparative lygina du objektus. Superlative išskiria vieną objektą iš grupės. Tas pats skirtumas galioja ir adverbs.
Main rule / explanation: Comparative: faster, more carefully, better than. Superlative: the fastest, the most carefully, the best. Kai kurios formos yra netaisyklingos.
Form / structure: Adjective/adverb + -er / more. Superlative: the + -est / the most. Irregular: good → better → the best; badly → worse → the worst.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai lyginame du daiktus / veiksmus arba išskiriame vieną daiktą / veiksmą iš grupės.
Examples:
My dog is faster than yours. → Mano šuo greitesnis už tavąjį.
This book is more interesting than that one. → Ši knyga įdomesnė už tą.
Anna runs faster than me. → Anna bėga greičiau už mane.
This is the best cake. → Tai geriausias pyragas.
He sings the most beautifully in the group. → Jis grupėje dainuoja gražiausiai.
Special cases / exceptions: Nemaišyk adjective ir adverb modelių. Good → adjective; well → adverb. Kai kurie žodžiai turi irregular forms.
Common mistakes:
❌ She works more quick. → ✅ She works more quickly.
❌ This is the better option of all three. → ✅ This is the best option of the three.
❌ He is more better. → ✅ He is better.
Don't confuse with: Comparative = 2. Superlative = 1 from a group. Žiūrėk, ar apibūdini noun, ar action.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Comparative → two.
Superlative → group.
Adjective and adverb may use different forms.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: No longer, any longer ir anymore nurodo, kad kažkas nustojo būti tiesa.
Main rule / explanation: No longer reiškia „daugiau ne“. Any longer/anymore paprastai vartojami neigiamame sakinyje: not ... any longer / not ... anymore.
Form / structure: No longer + verb. Do/does not + verb + anymore/any longer.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai sakome, kad kažkas daugiau nebevyksta arba nebėra tiesa.
Examples:
I no longer play that game. → Aš daugiau nebežaidžiu to žaidimo.
We don't watch cartoons anymore. → Mes daugiau nebežiūrime animacinių filmukų.
She doesn't live here any longer. → Ji čia daugiau nebegyvena.
He no longer wears glasses. → Jis daugiau nebedėvi akinių.
Special cases / exceptions: Žodžių vieta svarbi: no longer paprastai eina prieš pagrindinį veiksmažodį, o anymore/any longer – paprastai po tarinio neigiamoje konstrukcijoje.
Common mistakes:
❌ I work no longer there. → ✅ I no longer work there.
❌ I no longer don't work there. → ✅ I no longer work there.
❌ I work there anymore. → ✅ I don't work there anymore.
Don't confuse with: Nenaudok anymore kaip laisvo no longer pakaitalo bet kurioje pozicijoje. Žiūrėk į sakinio struktūrą.
Quick summary / memory hook:
no longer + verb.
not + verb + anymore/any longer.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: However, although, because, so, and time connectors
Core idea: Šie žodžiai sieja idėjas, bet atlieka skirtingas funkcijas: contrast, reason, result arba time.
Main rule / explanation: Although įveda contrast konstrukcijos viduje. However sieja kontrastuojančias idėjas tarp sakinių / dalių. Because = priežastis. So = rezultatas. When/while/before/after/as soon as/until = laikas.
Form / structure: Although + clause. Sentence. However, sentence. because + reason. so + result. Time connector + clause.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai siejame idėjas ir parodome kontrastą, priežastį, rezultatą arba laiką.
Examples:
Although it was raining, we went outside. → Nors lijo, išėjome į lauką.
It was raining. However, we went outside. → Lijo. Tačiau išėjome į lauką.
We stayed home because it was cold. → Likome namuose, nes buvo šalta.
It was late, so we went home. → Buvo vėlu, todėl grįžome namo.
When Mum arrives, we'll eat. → Kai mama grįš, mes valgysime.
Special cases / exceptions: Although ir however neturi tokios pačios gramatikos. Nedėk however ten, kur reikia although konstrukcijos.
Common mistakes:
❌ Although it was late. However, we continued. (ne viena konstrukcija) → ✅ Although it was late, we continued.
❌ We stayed, so we needed more time. → ✅ We stayed because we needed more time. / We needed more time, so we stayed.
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia nustatyk ryšį: contrast, reason, result arba time.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Although/however = contrast.
because = reason.
so = result.
time connectors = sequence.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Prepositions of movement: Along, across, over, etc.
Core idea: Prepositions of movement parodo judėjimo kelią, o ne tik vietą.
Main rule / explanation: Along – judėjimas išilgai. Across – iš vienos pusės į kitą. Through – per vidinę erdvę. Over – virš / per kliūtį.
Form / structure: move/walk/run + along/across/through/over + noun.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai aprašome judėjimo kelią: palei ką nors, per erdvę, iš vienos pusės į kitą arba per kliūtį.
Examples:
We walked along the river. → Ėjome palei upę.
We ran across the street. → Perbėgome gatvę.
The train went through the tunnel. → Traukinys pravažiavo per tunelį.
The cat jumped over the box. → Katė peršoko per dėžę.
Special cases / exceptions: Prielinksnį rinkis pagal judėjimo trajektoriją, o ne pagal vieną lietuvišką vertimą „per“.
Common mistakes:
❌ We walked through the street. (jei reikšmė – iš vienos gatvės pusės į kitą) → ✅ We walked across the street.
❌ The train went across the tunnel. → ✅ The train went through the tunnel.
Don't confuse with: Along = palei. Across = iš vienos pusės į kitą. Through = per vidinę erdvę. Over = virš / per kliūtį.
Quick summary / memory hook:
along = palei.
across = iš vienos pusės į kitą.
through = per vidinę erdvę.
over = per / virš.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: On time vs In time, At the end vs In the end.
Core idea: On time ir in time yra panašūs, bet vienas susijęs su tvarkaraščiu, o kitas – su tuo, ar spėjome iki reikiamo momento. At the end ir in the end taip pat skiriasi.
Main rule / explanation: On time = tiksliai laiku pagal tvarkaraštį. In time = pakankamai anksti, kad nepavėluotume į įvykį. At the end = laikotarpio / vietos / įvykio pabaigoje. In the end = galiausiai.
Form / structure: on time = schedule. in time + for/to = before too late. at the end of + period/event. in the end = finally.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai reikia atskirti „laiku pagal tvarkaraštį“, „spėti“, „pabaigoje“ ir „galiausiai“.
Examples:
The school bus arrived on time. → Mokyklos autobusas atvyko laiku.
We arrived in time for the film. → Atvykome pakankamai anksti į filmą.
At the end of the story, the hero went home. → Istorijos pabaigoje herojus grįžo namo.
In the end, we chose the blue team. → Galiausiai pasirinkome mėlyną komandą.
Special cases / exceptions: Pagrindinė užuomina: schedule → on time. Enough early → in time. Final part → at the end. Final result/decision → in the end.
Common mistakes:
❌ The train arrived in time. (jei svarbus tvarkaraštis) → ✅ The train arrived on time.
❌ At the end, she accepted the offer. → ✅ In the end, she accepted the offer.
Don't confuse with: Neversk šių posakių pažodžiui. Mokykis jų kaip paruoštų porų.
Quick summary / memory hook:
on time = pagal tvarkaraštį.
in time = ne per vėlai.
at the end = pabaigoje.
in the end = galiausiai.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Asking questions in English: Question forms
Core idea: Anglų kalbos klausimai turi savo struktūrą. Paprastai auxiliary arba be eina prieš subject.
Main rule / explanation: Yes/no questions: be/auxiliary + subject. Wh-questions: question word + auxiliary/be + subject + main verb. Modal questions: modal + subject + V1.
Form / structure: Are you ready? Do you work here? Did she call? Where do they live? Why is he late? Can you help?
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai užduodame įprastus Yes/No ir Wh-klausimus ir reikia teisingai parinkti pagalbinį veiksmažodį.
Examples:
Do you like music? → Ar tau patinka muzika?
Where does Sam live? → Kur gyvena Samas?
What are they doing? → Ką jie daro?
Can you help me? → Ar gali man padėti?
Why is the dog barking? → Kodėl šuo loja?
Special cases / exceptions: Įprastame direct question auxiliary lieka prieš subject. Nekopijuok įprasto teiginio žodžių tvarkos.
Common mistakes:
❌ Where they live? → ✅ Where do they live?
❌ Why she is late? → ✅ Why is she late?
❌ What you need? → ✅ What do you need?
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia rask auxiliary/be/modal. Tada subject. Tada main verb, jei jo reikia.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Auxiliary/be before subject.
Wh-word comes first in Wh-questions.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Jei who/what yra subject, klausimas sudaromas kitaip: paprastai do/does/did nereikia. Jei who/what yra object, reikia auxiliary. Prielinksnis šnekamojoje anglų kalboje dažnai eina į sakinio pabaigą.
Main rule / explanation: Subject question: Who called you? Object question: Who did you call? Preposition often at the end: Who did you speak to?
Form / structure: Subject question: Who/What + verb ...? Object question: Who/What + do/does/did + subject + V1 ...? + preposition at end if needed.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai who/what yra veiksmo atlikėjas arba kai who/what yra objektas ir klausime yra prielinksnis.
Examples:
Who called you? → Kas tau paskambino?
Who did you call? → Kam paskambinai?
What happened? → Kas atsitiko?
Who did you speak to? → Su kuo kalbėjai?
What are you looking at? → Į ką žiūri?
Special cases / exceptions: Nedėk did, jei who/what jau yra subject: Who called? – normali neutrali forma. Formaliojoje kalboje galima To whom did you speak?, bet everyday English dažniau vartojama Who did you speak to?
Common mistakes:
❌ Who did call you? → ✅ Who called you?
❌ What did happen? → ✅ What happened? (įprastas neutralus variantas)
❌ To who did you speak? → ✅ Who did you speak to? / To whom did you speak?
Don't confuse with: Pirmas klausimas: who/what atlieka veiksmą ar jį gauna? Jei atlieka, paprastai vartojame be do/does/did.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Who/what as subject → usually no do/does/did.
Who/what as object → auxiliary needed.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Present Simple ir Present Continuous abu aprašo dabartį, tačiau Simple rodo įprastą / stabilią situaciją, o Continuous – veiksmą dabar, laikiną ar besikeičiančią situaciją.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple – įpročiai, rutina, faktai ir stabilios būsenos. Present Continuous = am/is/are + V-ing veiksmui, vykstančiam dabar, laikinam ar besikeičiančiam procesui.
Form / structure: S + V1/V-s. S + am/is/are + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Palygink: I work with sales data. / I'm working with sales data this week.
Examples:
I usually start work at eight. → Paprastai pradedu darbą aštuntą.
Our office opens at nine. → Mūsų biuras atsidaro devintą.
I'm working from home this week. → Šią savaitę dirbu iš namų.
Special cases / exceptions: Stative verbs, tokie kaip know, believe, understand, need ir belong, dažnai vartojami Simple.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am know the answer. → ✅ I know the answer.
❌ He work from home this week. → ✅ He is working from home this week.
Don't confuse with: routine/stable ar temporary/in progress?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Simple = routine/fact/stable.
Continuous = now/temporary/changing.
Stative verbs → paprastai Simple.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Future forms – will, be going to, present continuous
Core idea: Trys ateities formos pirmiausia skiriasi reikšme: sprendimas / pažadas, jau suformuotas ketinimas arba suplanuotas susitarimas.
Main rule / explanation: Will – spontaniškas sprendimas, pasiūlymas, pažadas, prognozė. Going to – jau priimtas ketinimas ir prognozė pagal dabartinius požymius. Present Continuous – suplanuotas įvykis.
Form / structure: will + V1. am/is/are + going to + V1. am/is/are + V-ing + future time.
When / why we use it: I'll call her. = decision/promise. I'm going to call her. = intention. I'm calling her at three. = arrangement.
Examples:
The phone is ringing. I'll answer it. → Telefonas skamba. Atsiliepsiu.
We're going to change the process. → Ketiname pakeisti procesą.
I'm meeting the client at three tomorrow. → Rytoj trečią valandą susitinku su klientu.
Special cases / exceptions: Formos gali persidengti. Rinkis pagal kalbėtojo reikšmę, o ne vien pagal laiko žodį.
Common mistakes:
❌ I will to call her. → ✅ I will call her.
❌ She going to change it. → ✅ She is going to change it.
Don't confuse with: Will = decision/promise/prediction. Going to = intention/evidence. Present Continuous = arranged event.
Quick summary / memory hook:
will → sprendimas / pažadas / prognozė.
going to → ketinimas / požymis.
Present Continuous → susitarimas.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Past Simple sieja įvykį su užbaigtu praeities laiku. Present Perfect sieja praeitį su dabartimi arba kalba apie patirtį be užbaigto laiko.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple – completed event in finished past time. Present Perfect – experience, recent result or unfinished period connected with now.
Form / structure: Past Simple: V2 / did + V1. Present Perfect: have/has + V3.
When / why we use it: I visited Prague last year. = užbaigta praeitis. I've visited Prague three times. = patirtis.
Examples:
I worked in Germany in 2023. → 2023 metais dirbau Vokietijoje.
I've worked abroad several times. → Esu kelis kartus dirbęs užsienyje.
She has just finished the report. → Ji ką tik baigė ataskaitą.
Special cases / exceptions: Yesterday, last month, in 2020, two days ago paprastai reikalauja Past Simple. Ever, never, before, so far dažnai vartojami su Present Perfect, kai nėra finished time.
Common mistakes:
❌ I've seen him yesterday. → ✅ I saw him yesterday.
❌ I have visited Rome in 2020. → ✅ I visited Rome in 2020.
Don't confuse with: Finished past time → Past Simple. Experience/current connection → Present Perfect.
Quick summary / memory hook:
finished time → Past Simple.
experience/result/unfinished period → Present Perfect.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Present perfect simple and present perfect continuous
Core idea: Present Perfect Simple dažniau rodo rezultatą, veiksmų skaičių arba pasiekimą. Present Perfect Continuous labiau pabrėžia procesą, trukmę ar neseną veiklą.
Main rule / explanation: Simple = have/has + V3. Continuous = have/has been + V-ing.
Form / structure: Present Perfect Simple: have/has + V3. Present Perfect Continuous: have/has been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: I've written three emails. = result/number. I've been writing emails all morning. = activity/duration.
Examples:
I've cleaned the room. → Sutvarkiau kambarį.
I've been cleaning the room. → Tvarkiau kambarį.
She has written five messages. → Ji parašė penkias žinutes.
Special cases / exceptions: Stative verbs paprastai vartojami Simple: I've known her for years. Nesirink Continuous vien todėl, kad veiksmas trunka ilgai.
Common mistakes:
❌ I've been knowing her for years. → ✅ I've known her for years.
❌ I have been write emails. → ✅ I have been writing emails.
Don't confuse with: Simple → result/number/achievement. Continuous → activity/duration/recent process.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have/has + V3 = rezultatas / kiekis.
have/has been + V-ing = procesas / trukmė.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: During, for ir while susiję su laiku, tačiau po jų vartojamos skirtingos konstrukcijos.
Main rule / explanation: During + noun/period/event. For + length of time. While + clause with subject + verb.
Form / structure: during + noun. for + period of time. while + S + V.
When / why we use it: During the meeting. For two hours. While I was working.
Examples:
I fell asleep during the film. → Užmigau per filmą.
We talked for an hour. → Kalbėjomės valandą.
She called while I was driving. → Ji paskambino, kol vairavau.
Special cases / exceptions: Nedėk for tiesiai prieš pilną šalutinį sakinį.
Common mistakes:
❌ for I was working → ✅ while I was working.
❌ during two hours → ✅ for two hours.
Don't confuse with: During = per ką? For = kiek laiko? While = tuo metu, kai + sakinys.
Quick summary / memory hook:
during + noun.
for + duration.
while + clause.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs
Core idea: Comparative lygina du objektus, o superlative išskiria didžiausią arba mažiausią rezultatą grupėje. Tai galioja ir adjectives, ir adverbs.
Main rule / explanation: Comparatives: faster, more carefully, better than. Superlatives: the fastest, the most carefully. Prieveiksmiai dažnai vartojami su more/most.
Form / structure: Comparative: -er / more + form + than. Superlative: the + -est / the most + form.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai lyginame du objektus arba pasirenkame vieną iš grupės.
Examples:
This version is more stable than the old one. → Ši versija yra stabilesnė už senąją.
She works more efficiently now. → Dabar ji dirba efektyviau.
He is the most experienced analyst. → Jis yra labiausiai patyręs analitikas.
Special cases / exceptions: Kai kurios formos yra irregular patterns: well → better → best. Po linking verbs reikia adjective, o apibūdinant veiksmą – adverb.
Common mistakes:
❌ She works more quick. → ✅ She works more quickly.
❌ He is most experienced analyst. → ✅ He is the most experienced analyst.
Don't confuse with: Paklausk: ar apibūdinu noun/person/state, ar action?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Comparative → two.
Superlative → group.
Adjective ≠ adverb.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: A/an, the ir article nebuvimas priklauso nuo to, ar daiktas konkretus ar bendras, ar jis žinomas klausytojui ir ar daiktavardis yra singular countable.
Main rule / explanation: A/an – singular countable, kai daiktas nėra konkretus arba minimas pirmą kartą. The – konkretus / žinomas. No article – dažnai plural ir uncountable bendrąja reikšme.
Form / structure: a/an + singular countable. the + specific noun. Ø + plural/uncountable general noun.
When / why we use it: I bought a laptop. The laptop was expensive. Laptops are useful.
Examples:
I bought a laptop yesterday. → Vakar nusipirkau nešiojamąjį kompiuterį.
The laptop is on my desk. → Nešiojamasis kompiuteris yra ant mano stalo.
Laptops are useful tools. → Nešiojamieji kompiuteriai yra naudingi įrankiai.
Technology changes quickly. → Technologijos greitai keičiasi.
Special cases / exceptions: Article pasirinkimas priklauso nuo prasmės ir konteksto, o ne tik nuo vertimo.
Common mistakes:
❌ I bought laptop. → ✅ I bought a laptop.
❌ A laptop was expensive. → ✅ The laptop was expensive.
Don't confuse with: a = vienas, bet nekonkretus. the = konkretus / žinomas. Ø = bendra plural/uncountable reikšmė.
Quick summary / memory hook:
a/an = singular non-specific.
the = specific/known.
Ø = general plural/uncountable.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Another, other, others, the other, the others
Core idea: Another, other, others, the other ir the others skiriasi pagal skaičių, daiktavardžio buvimą ir konkretumą.
Main rule / explanation: Another = dar vienas. Other eina prieš noun. Others – pronoun. The other – antras iš dviejų / konkretus likęs. The others – kiti žinomos grupės nariai.
Form / structure: another + singular noun. other + noun. others — be noun. the other + singular. the others — be noun.
When / why we use it: Some agreed; others disagreed. One file is correct; the other is broken.
Examples:
Can I have another question? → Ar galiu užduoti dar vieną klausimą?
We need other options. → Mums reikia kitų variantų.
Some agreed; others disagreed. → Kai kurie sutiko, kiti nesutiko.
The others are ready. → Kiti / likusieji yra pasiruošę.
Special cases / exceptions: Other kaip adjective paprastai reikalauja noun: other ideas. Others jau pakeičia noun.
Common mistakes:
❌ others ideas → ✅ other ideas.
❌ one file... another is broken → ✅ the other is broken.
Don't confuse with: Noun buvimas – svarbi užuomina: other + noun, others be noun.
Quick summary / memory hook:
another = dar vienas.
other + noun.
others = kiti.
the other = antras / likęs.
the others = likusieji.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Can, could, be able to – ability and possibility
Core idea: Can, could ir be able to reiškia gebėjimą arba galimybę, tačiau vartojami skirtingais laikais ir situacijose.
Main rule / explanation: Can – present ability/possibility. Could – past general ability ir polite requests. Be able to patogu, kai reikia kitos tense/construction.
Form / structure: can + V1. could + V1. be able to + V1.
When / why we use it: Can = gebėjimas dabar. Could = bendras gebėjimas praeityje arba mandagus prašymas. Be able to leidžia sudaryti future/perfect forms.
Examples:
I can drive. → Moku vairuoti.
I could swim at five. → Būdamas penkerių mokėjau plaukti.
Could you help me? → Ar galėtumėte man padėti?
I'll be able to join later. → Vėliau galėsiu prisijungti.
Special cases / exceptions: Vienam konkrečiam sėkmingam veiksmui praeityje was/were able to gali pabrėžti sėkmingą atlikimą.
Common mistakes:
❌ I can to drive. → ✅ I can drive.
❌ I'll can join later. → ✅ I'll be able to join later.
Don't confuse with: Modal → V1. Ateičiai ir kitoms konstrukcijoms vartojame be able to.
Quick summary / memory hook:
can = present ability.
could = past general ability/polite request.
be able to = flexible form.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: have to, must, should – obligation, prohibition, necessity, advice
Core idea: Have to, must ir should susiję su pareiga ir patarimu, tačiau skiriasi reikalavimo stiprumas ir šaltinis.
Main rule / explanation: Have to – pareiga dėl taisyklės / situacijos. Must – stipri būtinybė. Should – patarimas arba lūkestis.
Form / structure: have to + V1. must + V1. should + V1. Negative: don't have to / mustn't / shouldn't.
When / why we use it: Have to dažnai kyla iš taisyklės ar situacijos. Must yra stipri pareiga. Should yra patarimas.
Examples:
We have to wear ID badges. → Turime nešioti darbuotojo korteles.
You must keep this information private. → Privalai laikyti šią informaciją konfidencialią.
You should check the figures. → Turėtum patikrinti skaičius.
Special cases / exceptions: Don't have to = nėra pareigos. Mustn't = draudimas. Shouldn't = patarimas to nedaryti.
Common mistakes:
❌ You don't have to share it = „tau draudžiama“. → Ne: „tau nebūtina“.
❌ She must to check. → ✅ She must check.
Don't confuse with: Have to/must = obligation. Should = advice. Nepainiok don't have to ir mustn't.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have to = pareiga.
must = stipri būtinybė.
should = patarimas.
don't have to ≠ mustn't.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Reflexive pronouns rodo, kad subject ir object yra tas pats asmuo / daiktas; kartais jie tiesiog pabrėžia subject.
Main rule / explanation: Formos: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. By + reflexive gali reikšti alone.
Form / structure: subject + verb + reflexive. by + reflexive.
When / why we use it: Tas pats asmuo: She hurt herself. Pabrėžimas: I did it myself. Vienas: I did it by myself.
Examples:
She hurt herself. → Ji susižeidė.
I did it myself. → Aš pats tai padariau.
We solved the problem ourselves. → Mes patys išsprendėme problemą.
He travelled by himself. → Jis keliavo vienas.
Special cases / exceptions: Nenaudok reflexive pronoun vietoje paprasto object pronoun vien dėl formalumo.
Common mistakes:
❌ Please contact myself. → ✅ Please contact me.
❌ She told himself. → ✅ She told herself.
Don't confuse with: Reflexive = tas pats asmuo kaip subject arba pabrėžimas. Ordinary object pronoun = me/him/her.
Quick summary / memory hook:
myself/yourself/... = pats save / pats.
by myself = vienas.
Jais nepakeičiame įprastų object pronouns.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: -ed ir -ing adjectives sudaryti iš veiksmažodžių, bet apibūdina skirtingus dalykus: žmogaus jausmą arba to jausmo priežastį.
Main rule / explanation: -ed paprastai apibūdina, kaip žmogus jaučiasi. -ing paprastai apibūdina žmogų / daiktą, sukeliantį tą jausmą.
Form / structure: -ed adjective: bored, interested, confused. -ing adjective: boring, interesting, confusing.
When / why we use it: The task is confusing; the employees are confused.
Examples:
I'm bored. → Man nuobodu.
The film is boring. → Filmas nuobodus.
The task is confusing. → Užduotis paini.
The employees are confused. → Darbuotojai pasimetę.
Special cases / exceptions: I am boring reiškia „aš esu nuobodus / keliu nuobodulį“, o ne „man nuobodu“.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am boring. → ✅ I am bored.
❌ The lesson is bored. → ✅ The lesson is boring.
Don't confuse with: -ed = žmogaus jausmas / būsena. -ing = daikto ar situacijos sukeliama priežastis / savybė.
Quick summary / memory hook:
-ed → kaip aš jaučiuosi.
-ing → kas sukelia jausmą.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Past simple, past continuous, past perfect
Core idea: Pasakojant apie praeitį trys formos gali veikti kartu: Past Simple rodo pagrindinius įvykius, Past Continuous – foną / procesą, Past Perfect – tai, kas įvyko dar anksčiau.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple = completed event. Past Continuous = action in progress/background. Past Perfect = earlier event before another past event.
Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3.
When / why we use it: The meeting started. People were talking. The manager had left before I arrived.
Examples:
The meeting started at nine. → Susitikimas prasidėjo devintą.
People were talking when the manager arrived. → Žmonės kalbėjosi, kai atėjo vadovas.
The manager had left before I arrived. → Vadovas buvo išėjęs prieš man atvykstant.
Special cases / exceptions: Past Perfect reikalingas santykiniam įvykių eiliškumui praeityje parodyti, o ne tiesiog „labai senai“ praeičiai.
Common mistakes:
❌ Every past sentence should be Past Perfect. → Ne: reikia atsižvelgti į santykinį earlier event.
❌ I had went. → ✅ I had gone.
Don't confuse with: Timeline: earlier event → Past Perfect; background → Past Continuous; main completed event → Past Simple.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Perfect = anksčiau.
Past Continuous = procesas / fonas.
Past Simple = pagrindinis įvykis.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Review of all intermediate verb tenses (CEFR B1)
Core idea: Tai pagrindinių intermediate verb tenses sisteminimas. Svarbiausias įgūdis – rinktis laiką pagal reikšmę, o ne mechaniškai pagal signalinių žodžių sąrašą.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple – routine/fact/stable. Present Continuous – current/temporary. Past Simple – completed past. Past Continuous – past process. Past Perfect – earlier past. Present Perfect – past connected to now. Present Perfect Continuous – activity/duration to now. Future forms turi skirtingas meanings.
Form / structure: V1/V-s; am/is/are + V-ing; V2; was/were + V-ing; had + V3; have/has + V3; have/has been + V-ing; will/going to/Present Continuous.
When / why we use it: Žiūrėk į relationship: usual, now, finished past, process in past, earlier past, connection with now, duration to now arba future meaning.
Examples:
I usually work from home. → Paprastai dirbu iš namų.
I'm working at the office today. → Šiandien dirbu biure.
I finished the report yesterday. → Vakar baigiau ataskaitą.
I've already sent it. → Jau išsiunčiau.
I was checking the data when my manager called. → Tikrinau duomenis, kai paskambino mano vadovas.
Special cases / exceptions: Nesirink tense tik pagal vieną time expression. Pirmiausia nustatyk meaning and relationship.
Common mistakes:
❌ today = visada Present Continuous. → Ne.
❌ yesterday = vienintelis pasirinkimo pagrindas. → Žiūrėk į visą kontekstą.
Don't confuse with: Ši pamoka – sistemos žemėlapis, o ne naujas atskiras tense.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Routine → Present Simple.
Now/temp → Present Continuous.
Finished past → Past Simple.
Past process → Past Continuous.
Past before past → Past Perfect.
Past + now → Present Perfect.
Activity/duration + now → Present Perfect Continuous.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: usually, used to, be used to, get used to
Core idea: Usually, used to, be used to ir get used to panašūs, bet reiškia skirtingus dalykus: dabartinį įprastumą, seną įprotį arba pripratimo procesą.
Main rule / explanation: Usually – adverb of frequency. Used to + V1 – senas įprotis / būsena. Be used to + noun/-ing – būti pripratusiam. Get used to + noun/-ing – priprasti.
Form / structure: usually + verb. used to + V1. be used to + noun/V-ing. get used to + noun/V-ing.
When / why we use it: I usually work at home. = paprastai. I used to live there. = anksčiau. I'm used to working late. = esu pripratęs. I'm getting used to the new system. = priprantu.
Examples:
I usually work at home. → Paprastai dirbu namuose.
I used to live there. → Anksčiau ten gyvenau.
I'm used to working late. → Esu pripratęs dirbti iki vėlumos.
I'm getting used to the new system. → Priprantu prie naujos sistemos.
Special cases / exceptions: Po be/get used to reikia noun arba V-ing, ne infinitive.
Common mistakes:
❌ I'm used to work late. → ✅ I'm used to working late.
❌ I used to working late. → ✅ I used to work late.
Don't confuse with: used to = anksčiau. be used to = jau pripratęs. get used to = pripratimo procesas. usually = paprastai.
Quick summary / memory hook:
usually = now habit.
used to + V1 = past habit/state.
be used to + noun/-ing = accustomed.
get used to + noun/-ing = become accustomed.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Passive rodo veiksmą / rezultatą, kai atlikėjas nesvarbus, nežinomas arba nėra pagrindinis dėmesys.
Main rule / explanation: Passive = form of be + V3. Būtent be rodo laiką: is done, was done, has been done, will be done.
Form / structure: Present: is/are + V3. Past: was/were + V3. Perfect: has/have been + V3. Future: will be + V3.
When / why we use it: Renkamės passive, kai svarbiau veiksmas / rezultatas nei atlikėjas. By + agent pridedame, jei atlikėjas svarbus.
Examples:
The data is stored securely. → Duomenys saugiai saugomi.
The documents were signed yesterday. → Dokumentai buvo pasirašyti vakar.
The results will be published tomorrow. → Rezultatai bus paskelbti rytoj.
The report was prepared by the finance team. → Ataskaitą parengė finansų komanda.
Special cases / exceptions: Be + V3 būtina norint sudaryti pilną passive.
Common mistakes:
❌ The report written yesterday. → ✅ The report was written yesterday.
❌ The results will published tomorrow. → ✅ The results will be published tomorrow.
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia nustatyk be formos tense, tada V3.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Passive = be + V3.
Tense lives in be.
by + agent – kai atlikėjas svarbus.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Active voice sutelkia dėmesį į tai, kas atlieka veiksmą. Passive voice – į objektą / rezultatą, kuris gauna veiksmą.
Main rule / explanation: Active: subject performs action. Passive: subject receives action; active sakinio object tampa grammatical subject.
Form / structure: Active: The analyst prepared the report. Passive: The report was prepared by the analyst.
When / why we use it: Actor/action important → active. Result/affected object important → passive.
Examples:
The company launched the product. → Įmonė išleido produktą.
The product was launched in June. → Produktas buvo išleistas birželį.
The analyst prepared the report. → Analitikas parengė ataskaitą.
The report was prepared by the analyst. → Ataskaitą parengė analitikas.
Special cases / exceptions: Paversdami active į passive turime pertvarkyti subject/object, o ne tik pridėti be.
Common mistakes: ❌ The analyst was prepared the report. → ✅ The report was prepared by the analyst.
Don't confuse with: Ko norime pagrindiniu dėmesiu? Actor → active. Result/object → passive.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Active = kas atliko.
Passive = kas / kas buvo padaryta.
Passive reikalauja pertvarkymo.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Modal verbs of deduction – must, might, could, can’t
Core idea: Modal deduction vartoja must, might, could ir can't ne taisyklei, o loginei išvadai pagal turimus požymius.
Main rule / explanation: Must = stipri išvada. Might/could = galimas paaiškinimas. Can't = stipri išvada, kad kažkas neįmanoma.
Form / structure: must/might/could/can't + V1 arba be.
When / why we use it: The lights are on, so they must be inside. = stipri išvada. He might be asleep. = galimybė. This can't be the final version. = stipri išvada, kad neįmanoma.
Examples:
The lights are on, so they must be inside. → Šviesos įjungtos, vadinasi, jie turėtų būti viduje.
He might be asleep. → Galbūt jis miega.
This can't be the final version. → Tai negali būti galutinė versija.
Special cases / exceptions: Čia must reiškia deduction, o ne obligation. Reikšmę lemia kontekstas.
Common mistakes:
❌ He must be inside = visada „jis privalo būti viduje“. → Čia tai gali būti loginė išvada.
❌ He might to be asleep. → ✅ He might be asleep.
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia paklausk: tai taisyklė ar išvada pagal evidence? Jei išvada – modal deduction.
Quick summary / memory hook:
must = stipri išvada.
might/could = galbūt.
can't = negali būti.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: First Conditional ir future time clauses kalba apie realistinę ateitį. Po when/before/after/as soon as/until šalutiniame sakinyje paprastai vartojamas Present, nors prasmė yra ateities.
Main rule / explanation: First Conditional: if + Present Simple, will + V1. Future time clause: connector + Present form; main clause can contain will.
Form / structure: If + Present Simple, will + V1. I'll + V1 + when/before/after/as soon as/until + Present Simple.
When / why we use it: Sąlyga: If the client agrees, we'll start. Laikas: I'll call when I arrive.
Examples:
If the client agrees, we'll start Monday. → Jei klientas sutiks, pradėsime pirmadienį.
I'll send the link as soon as I finish. → Išsiųsiu nuorodą, kai tik baigsiu.
I'll call when I arrive. → Paskambinsiu, kai atvyksiu.
Special cases / exceptions: Nedėk will po when/before/after/as soon as/until vien todėl, kad reikšmė yra ateities.
Common mistakes:
❌ When I will arrive, I'll call. → ✅ When I arrive, I'll call.
❌ If the client will agree, we'll start. → ✅ If the client agrees, we'll start.
Don't confuse with: if-clause = condition. time clause = when the event happens. Abi dependent clauses ateities reikšme vartoja Present.
Quick summary / memory hook:
if + Present → will + V1.
when/before/after/as soon as/until + Present → future meaning.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Second Conditional rodo hipotetinę, mažai tikėtiną arba įsivaizduojamą situaciją dabartyje / ateityje.
Main rule / explanation: Forma: if + Past Simple, would + V1. Past forma čia rodo atstumą nuo tikrovės.
Form / structure: If + V2, would + V1. Advice pattern: If I were you, I'd...
When / why we use it: Naudojame imaginary/unlikely situations apibūdinti.
Examples:
If I had more time, I'd study German. → Jei turėčiau daugiau laiko, mokyčiausi vokiečių kalbos.
If she were here, she'd know what to do. → Jei ji būtų čia, žinotų, ką daryti.
If I were you, I'd wait. → Tavo vietoje palaukčiau.
Special cases / exceptions: If I were you – įprasta pastovi konstrukcija. Were gali būti vartojama formaliose hypothetical clauses.
Common mistakes:
❌ If I would have more time... → ✅ If I had more time...
❌ If she were here, she will help. → ✅ If she were here, she'd help.
Don't confuse with: Past form ≠ būtinai past time. Čia ji rodo hypothetical distance.
Quick summary / memory hook:
If + Past Simple → would + V1.
Imaginary/unlikely now/future.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: First ir Second Conditional skiriasi tuo, kaip kalbėtojas mato sąlygą: kaip realią galimybę arba hipotetinę / mažai tikėtiną situaciją.
Main rule / explanation: First = realistic possibility. Second = hypothetical/unlikely situation.
Form / structure: First: if + Present, will + V1. Second: if + Past, would + V1.
When / why we use it: Palygink: If we have enough time, we'll finish. / If we had more time, we'd redesign it.
Examples:
If we have enough time, we'll finish today. → Jei turėsime pakankamai laiko, šiandien baigsime.
If we had more time, we'd redesign it. → Jei turėtume daugiau laiko, tai perdarytume.
Special cases / exceptions: Nenaudok Second automatiškai bet kuriai neaiškiai situacijai. Svarbus kalbėtojo požiūris.
Common mistakes:
❌ If it rains, we'd cancel. → ✅ If it rains, we'll cancel. (reali galima ateitis → First Conditional.)
❌ If I knew it will rain, I would stay home. → ✅ If I knew it would rain, I would stay home. (sąlyga nereali / įsivaizduojama.)
Don't confuse with: First = real/possible. Second = imagined/unlikely.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Pirmiausia įvertink meaning.
Real possibility → First.
Hypothetical/unlikely → Second.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Third Conditional kalba apie nerealią praeitį: sąlyga neįvyko, todėl neįvyko ir įsivaizduojamas rezultatas.
Main rule / explanation: If + Past Perfect, would have + V3.
Form / structure: If + had + V3, would have + V3.
When / why we use it: Naudojame imagined past condition ir result išreikšti.
Examples:
If we had checked the data, we would have found the error. → Jei būtume patikrinę duomenis, būtume radę klaidą.
If she had left earlier, she would have caught the train. → Jei ji būtų išėjusi anksčiau, būtų suspėjusi į traukinį.
Special cases / exceptions: If-clause nenaudojame would have standard Third Conditional struktūroje.
Common mistakes:
❌ If we would have checked... → ✅ If we had checked...
❌ If she had left earlier, she would catch... → ✅ she would have caught...
Don't confuse with: Abu rezultatai priklauso praeičiai ir realybėje neįvyko.
Quick summary / memory hook:
if + had + V3 → would have + V3.
Imaginary past.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Reported Speech perteikia kito žmogaus žodžius be tikslios tiesioginės citatos. Prireikus keičiasi tense, pronouns ir time expressions.
Main rule / explanation: Po past reporting verb pradinis laikas dažnai pastumiamas atgal. Šiandien / rytoj ir įvardžiai gali keistis. Reported questions vartoja statement word order.
Form / structure: Direct → reported clause. Question: asked + question word + subject + verb.
When / why we use it: 'I work here.' → He said he worked there. 'Tomorrow' → the next day. She asked where I lived.
Examples:
Tom said, 'I need help.' → Tom said that he needed help. → Tomas pasakė, kad jam reikia pagalbos.
Anna said, 'I'll call tomorrow.' → Anna said she'd call the next day. → Anna pasakė, kad paskambins kitą dieną.
She asked where I lived. → Ji paklausė, kur aš gyvenu.
Special cases / exceptions: Backshift nėra mechaninė taisyklė visais atvejais. Reikšmė ir situacija svarbesnės už automatiką.
Common mistakes: ❌ She asked where did I live. → ✅ She asked where I lived.
Don't confuse with: Reported question išlaiko statement tvarką: where I lived, o ne where did I live.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Perpasakojame, o ne cituojame.
Stebėk tense, pronouns, time words.
Reported question → statement order.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Gerund or infinitive – do, to do, doing
Core idea: Po skirtingų veiksmažodžių reikia skirtingo pattern: to + V1, V-ing arba abiejų formų. Kartais formos pasirinkimas keičia reikšmę.
Main rule / explanation: Kai kurie verbs take infinitive, kiti gerund; kai kurie leidžia abi formas. Su remember, stop, try pattern pakeitimas gali pakeisti meaning.
Form / structure: verb + to + V1. verb + V-ing. Kai kurie verbs + both with meaning difference.
When / why we use it: Palygink: Remember to lock the door. / I remember locking the door. / Try to open it. / Try opening it.
Examples:
Remember to lock the door. → Nepamiršk užrakinti durų.
I remember locking the door. → Prisimenu, kad užrakinau duris.
Try to open it. → Pabandyk jį atidaryti.
Try opening it. → Pabandyk atidaryti (kaip būdą).
Special cases / exceptions: Formos nesirink vien pagal pirmojo verb vertimą. Žiūrėk į intended meaning.
Common mistakes:
❌ I remember to locking the door. → ✅ I remember locking the door.
❌ Try to opening it. → ✅ Try opening it.
Don't confuse with: Verb pattern yra konkretaus veiksmažodžio gramatikos dalis. Kartais jis keičia reikšmę.
Quick summary / memory hook:
remember + to do / doing ≠ tas pats.
stop/try taip pat gali keisti meaning.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Much, many, a lot, little, few, some, any, no – quantifiers
Core idea: Quantifiers rodo kiekį ir reikalauja tinkamo daiktavardžio tipo. Svarbu atskirti few/little ir a few/a little.
Main rule / explanation: Many, few, a lot of → plural countable. Much, little, a lot of → uncountable. Some dažnai positive; any – questions/negatives su išimtimis. No + noun = negative.
Form / structure: many/few + plural countable. much/little + uncountable. a lot of + both. some/any/no + appropriate noun.
When / why we use it: Rinkis quantifier po to, kai nustatai countable/uncountable ir norimą kiekio atspalvį.
Examples:
We have few options. → Turime mažai variantų.
There isn't much time. → Neturime daug laiko.
There are no seats left. → Laisvų vietų nebeliko.
I bought some fruit. → Nusipirkau šiek tiek vaisių.
Special cases / exceptions: Few/little dažnai reiškia „mažai, nepakankamai“. A few/a little skamba pozityviau: tam tikras kiekis yra.
Common mistakes:
❌ little options → ✅ few options.
❌ many information → ✅ much information.
❌ I don't have no time. → ✅ I don't have any time.
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia countable ar uncountable. Tada amount/meaning.
Quick summary / memory hook:
many/few → countable plural.
much/little → uncountable.
a few/a little → nedidelis, bet esantis kiekis.
no + noun = negative.

Core idea: All reiškia visą trijų ar daugiau narių grupę arba visą uncountable kiekį. Both vartojamas dviem.
Main rule / explanation: All employees / all the information. Both options / both of us. Both gali būti prieš plural noun arba po subject pronoun.
Form / structure: all + plural/uncountable. both + plural referring to two.
When / why we use it: 2 → both. 3+ arba uncountable whole → all.
Examples:
All the reports are ready. → Visos ataskaitos paruoštos.
Both answers are possible. → Abu atsakymai galimi.
They both understand the problem. → Jie abu supranta problemą.
Both of us agree. → Mes abu sutinkame.
Special cases / exceptions: Both pagrindine reikšme vartojamas tik dviem. All – trims ar daugiau arba visai uncountable masei.
Common mistakes: ❌ Both options, if there are five options. → ✅ All options.
Don't confuse with: Suskaičiuok grupės narius: 2 → both; 3+ / visa masė → all.
Quick summary / memory hook:
both = 2.
all = 3+ or whole mass.

Core idea: Both, either ir neither susiję su dviem variantais: abu, bet kuris iš dviejų arba nė vienas iš dviejų.
Main rule / explanation: Both = the two together. Either = one of two. Neither = not one and not the other.
Form / structure: both + plural. either + singular noun. neither + singular noun.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai yra būtent du variantai / objektai.
Examples:
Both solutions work. → Abu sprendimai veikia.
Either solution will work. → Tiks bet kuris iš dviejų sprendimų.
Neither solution works. → Nė vienas iš dviejų sprendimų netinka.
Special cases / exceptions: Basic meaning either/neither nevartojame trims ar daugiau variantų.
Common mistakes:
❌ Either of five options... → Pagrindinei reikšmei reikia kito quantifier.
❌ Neither options works. → ✅ Neither option works.
Don't confuse with: Tai dviejų elementų logika: both = 2, either = 1 iš 2, neither = 0 iš 2.
Quick summary / memory hook:
2 items:
both = 2 together.
either = 1 of 2.
neither = 0 of 2.

Core idea: Any, no ir none gali reikšti nebuvimą / neapibrėžtą kiekį, tačiau vartojami skirtingose konstrukcijose.
Main rule / explanation: Any + noun gali reikšti one/some/whichever pagal kontekstą. No + noun padaro sakinį neigiamą. None – pronoun, pakeičiantis noun phrase.
Form / structure: any + noun. no + noun. none without noun.
When / why we use it: There aren't any tickets. / There are no tickets. / None came.
Examples:
There aren't any tickets. → Nėra jokių bilietų.
There are no tickets. → Bilietų nėra.
I invited five people, but none came. → Pakviečiau penkis žmones, bet nė vienas neatėjo.
Special cases / exceptions: Standartinėje anglų kalboje vengiame double negative: I don't have any, ne I don't have none.
Common mistakes:
❌ I don't have none. → ✅ I don't have any. / I have none.
❌ None tickets are left. → ✅ No tickets are left.
Don't confuse with: no reikalauja noun. none pakeičia noun phrase.
Quick summary / memory hook:
any + noun.
no + noun.
none = pronoun.
No double negatives.

Lesson / Topic: So, such, such a, so much, so many
Core idea: So, such, so much ir so many stiprina laipsnį arba kiekį, bet po jų vartojamos skirtingos konstrukcijos.
Main rule / explanation: So + adjective/adverb. Such + noun phrase. So much + uncountable. So many + plural countable.
Form / structure: so + adj/adv. such + noun phrase. so much + uncountable. so many + plural countable.
When / why we use it: Palygink formą po so ir such: so difficult; such a difficult task.
Examples:
It was so cold. → Buvo taip šalta.
It was such a cold day. → Buvo tokia šalta diena.
We had so much work. → Turėjome tiek daug darbo.
There were so many emails. → Buvo tiek daug laiškų.
Special cases / exceptions: Po so negalima tiesiogiai dėti a + noun phrase: ne so a difficult task.
Common mistakes:
❌ so a difficult task → ✅ such a difficult task.
❌ so many work → ✅ so much work.
❌ such cold → ✅ so cold / such a cold day.
Don't confuse with: Jei iškart adjective/adverb → so. Jei noun phrase → such. Jei kiekis → so much/many.
Quick summary / memory hook:
so + adj/adv.
such + noun phrase.
so much + uncountable.
so many + plural countable.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Defining relative clause reikalinga noun identifikuoti. Non-defining prideda papildomą informaciją ir atskiriama kableliais.
Main rule / explanation: Defining = essential identifying information, no commas. Non-defining = extra information, commas. Who – people; which – things. That paprastai defining.
Form / structure: Defining: noun + who/which/that + clause. Non-defining: noun, who/which + clause,.
When / why we use it: Palygink: The report that you sent... ir My laptop, which is three years old,...
Examples:
The report that you sent is useful. → Ataskaita, kurią atsiuntei, yra naudinga.
My laptop, which is three years old, still works well. → Mano nešiojamasis kompiuteris, kuriam treji metai, vis dar gerai veikia.
The employee who joined yesterday needs access. → Darbuotojui, kuris prisijungė vakar, reikia prieigos.
Special cases / exceptions: Nedėk commas aplink essential identifying information. That paprastai nevartojamas standard non-defining clauses.
Common mistakes:
❌ My laptop, that is three years old,... → ✅ My laptop, which is three years old,...
❌ The employee, who joined yesterday, needs access. (jei clause identifikuoja darbuotoją) → ✅ The employee who joined yesterday needs access.
Don't confuse with: Defining = „kuris būtent?“. Non-defining = papildoma pastaba.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Defining = essential, no commas.
Non-defining = extra, commas.
who → people; which → things.

Lesson / Topic: Question tags: Aren't you? don't you?
Core idea: Question tag paverčia teiginį trumpu klausimu, kuriuo prašoma patvirtinimo: „tiesa?“ / „ar ne?“
Main rule / explanation: Positive statement paprastai gauna negative tag. Negative statement – positive tag. Naudojame tą patį auxiliary/modal ir tą patį subject pronoun.
Form / structure: Positive + negative tag. Negative + positive tag. Auxiliary/modal must match; with ordinary present/past use do/does/did.
When / why we use it: Pavyzdžiui: You're ready, aren't you? Jei teiginys neigiamas: You don't know, do you?
Examples:
You're ready, aren't you? → Tu pasiruošęs, tiesa?
You don't know, do you? → Tu nežinai, tiesa?
She can drive, can't she? → Ji moka vairuoti, tiesa?
They weren't late, were they? → Jie nepavėlavo, tiesa?
Special cases / exceptions: Tag turi sutapti su pagrindinio sakinio tense, auxiliary/modal ir subject pronoun.
Common mistakes:
❌ She can drive, doesn't she? → ✅ She can drive, can't she?
❌ They weren't late, weren't they? → ✅ They weren't late, were they?
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia rask auxiliary/modal pagrindiniame sakinyje, tada padaryk priešingą polarity.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Positive → negative tag.
Negative → positive tag.
Match auxiliary + tense + pronoun.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Clauses of contrast, purpose and reason
Core idea: Clauses of contrast, purpose ir reason atsako į skirtingus klausimus: nepaisant ko? kokiu tikslu? kodėl?
Main rule / explanation: Although/even though rodo netikėtą kontrastą. To/in order to/so that reiškia purpose. Because/since/as įveda reason.
Form / structure: although/even though + clause. to/in order to + V1. so that + clause. because/since/as + clause.
When / why we use it: Palygink goal ir cause: We left early to avoid traffic. / We changed the plan because the weather was bad.
Examples:
Although it was late, we continued. → Nors buvo vėlu, tęsėme.
We left early to avoid traffic. → Išėjome anksti, kad išvengtume spūsčių.
We changed the plan because the weather was bad. → Pakeitėme planą, nes oras buvo prastas.
Special cases / exceptions: Purpose ir reason nėra tas pats: purpose = goal; reason = cause.
Common mistakes:
❌ We left early because catch the train. → ✅ We left early to catch the train.
❌ We left early to the weather was bad. → ✅ We left early because the weather was bad.
Don't confuse with: Paklausk: what was the goal? → purpose. Why did it happen? → reason. Unexpected contrast? → although/even though.
Quick summary / memory hook:
contrast = although/even though.
purpose = to/in order to/so that.
reason = because/since/as.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Kai kurie verbs sudaro pastovų junginį su konkrečiu preposition. Šis preposition yra verb pattern dalis.
Main rule / explanation: Mokykis verb + preposition kaip visumos: depend on, listen to, wait for, belong to.
Form / structure: verb + preposition + noun/pronoun/V-ing as appropriate.
When / why we use it: Neversk preposition atskirai – mokykis viso chunk.
Examples:
It depends on the price. → Tai priklauso nuo kainos.
Please listen to me. → Prašau manęs pasiklausyti.
We're waiting for the client. → Laukiame kliento.
This bag belongs to Anna. → Šis krepšys priklauso Annai.
Special cases / exceptions: Prielinksnio dažnai negalima logiškai išversti vienas prie vieno iš lietuvių kalbos.
Common mistakes:
❌ listen me → ✅ listen to me.
❌ depend of → ✅ depend on.
❌ wait the client → ✅ wait for the client.
Don't confuse with: Mokykis ne tik verb. Mokykis verb + preposition kaip vieno leksinio ir gramatinio vieneto.
Quick summary / memory hook:
depend on.
listen to.
wait for.
belong to.
Mokykis chunk.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Daugeliui adjectives taip pat reikia konkretaus preposition. Tai pastovios konstrukcijos dalis.
Main rule / explanation: Dažni patterns: interested in, good at, afraid of, responsible for.
Form / structure: adjective + preposition + noun/pronoun/V-ing as appropriate.
When / why we use it: Tinkamo preposition dažnai negalima numatyti pagal lietuvišką vertimą.
Examples:
She's interested in analytics. → Ji domisi analitika.
He's good at explaining complex ideas. → Jis gerai moka paaiškinti sudėtingas idėjas.
I'm responsible for this report. → Aš atsakingas už šią ataskaitą.
She is afraid of making mistakes. → Ji bijo daryti klaidų.
Special cases / exceptions: Mokykis visą expression kartu, o ne tik adjective.
Common mistakes:
❌ interested on → ✅ interested in.
❌ good in explaining → ✅ good at explaining.
❌ responsible of → ✅ responsible for.
Don't confuse with: Preposition priklauso adjective pattern.
Quick summary / memory hook:
interested in.
good at.
afraid of.
responsible for.
Mokykis whole phrase.

Core idea: Had better ir It's time reiškia stiprų patarimą arba tai, kad dabar jau metas ką nors padaryti.
Main rule / explanation: Had better + V1 = stiprus patarimas su užuomina apie galimą neigiamą pasekmę. It's time + Past Simple = dabar jau metas.
Form / structure: had better + V1. had better not + V1. It's time + subject + Past Simple.
When / why we use it: You'd better save the file. = geriau išsaugok. It's time we started. = mums jau metas pradėti.
Examples:
You'd better save the file. → Tau geriau išsaugoti failą.
You'd better not miss the train. → Tau geriau nepraleisti traukinio.
It's time we started. → Mums jau metas pradėti.
Special cases / exceptions: Po had better vartojamas V1 be to. Past Simple po It's time nebūtinai reiškia praeitį.
Common mistakes:
❌ You'd better to leave. → ✅ You'd better leave.
❌ It's time we start. → ✅ It's time we started.
Don't confuse with: Had better stipresnis už įprastą should. It's time + Past Simple rodo, kad veiksmą jau reikėtų atlikti.
Quick summary / memory hook:
had better + V1.
had better not + V1.
It's time + Past Simple.

Lesson / Topic: for, since, from – what's the difference?
Core idea: For, since ir from rodo trukmę arba laikotarpio pradžią, bet atsako į skirtingus klausimus.
Main rule / explanation: For = duration. Since = starting point continuing to now/another reference time. From = starting point, dažnai su endpoint arba range.
Form / structure: for + length. since + starting point. from + starting point (+ to/until).
When / why we use it: For atsako „kiek laiko?“. Since – „nuo kada?“. From dažnai sudaro range.
Examples:
I've lived here for five years. → Čia gyvenu penkerius metus.
I've worked here since 2021. → Čia dirbu nuo 2021 metų.
The office is open from nine to five. → Biuras dirba nuo devynių iki penkių.
Special cases / exceptions: Nepainiok duration ir starting point.
Common mistakes:
❌ I've lived here since five years. → ✅ I've lived here for five years.
❌ I've worked here for 2021. → ✅ I've worked here since 2021.
Don't confuse with: for = amount of time. since = starting point. from = starting point/range.
Quick summary / memory hook:
for = how long.
since = from when.
from = starting point, often + to.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: B1 Phrasal verbs 1 – Exercises and explanation
Core idea: Phrasal verbs sujungia verb ir particle ir dažnai įgyja reikšmę, kurios negalima sudėti iš atskirų žodžių.
Main rule / explanation: Mokykis phrasal verb kartu su jo reikšme ir grammar pattern. Čia svarbūs get up, find out, look for, turn on, carry on.
Form / structure: verb + particle. Pattern priklauso nuo konkretaus phrasal verb.
When / why we use it: Žiūrėk į whole phrase ir kontekstą.
Examples:
I found out about the change yesterday. → Vakar sužinojau apie pakeitimą.
Please turn on the monitor. → Prašau įjunk monitorių.
We need to look for a solution. → Turime ieškoti sprendimo.
Please carry on. → Prašau tęsk.
Special cases / exceptions: Neversk kiekvieno žodžio atskirai: look for ≠ tiesiog look + for.
Common mistakes:
❌ Turn on = visada „pasukti“. → Ne: kontekste turn on = įjungti.
❌ look + for = įprastas pažodinis junginys. → Ne, look for = ieškoti.
Don't confuse with: Vienas particle pakeičia pagrindinio verb reikšmę.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Mokykis whole phrasal verb.
get up.
find out.
look for.
turn on.
carry on.

Lesson / Topic: B1 Phrasal verbs 2 – Exercises and explanation
Core idea: B1 lygyje svarbu žinoti ne tik phrasal verb reikšmę, bet ir ar object gali atskirti verb ir particle.
Main rule / explanation: Kai kurie phrasal verbs yra separable: pick the file up / pick up the file. Kiti inseparable: look after the child. Su pronoun separable object paprastai eina tarp verb ir particle.
Form / structure: separable: pick + object + up / pick up + object. With pronoun: pick it up. Inseparable: look after + object.
When / why we use it: Mokykis meaning + object pattern + separability.
Examples:
Please pick up the documents. → Prašau paimk dokumentus.
Please pick the documents up. → Prašau paimk dokumentus.
She looks after the new employee. → Ji prižiūri naują darbuotoją.
Pick it up. → Pakelk tai.
Special cases / exceptions: Su separable phrasal verbs pronoun paprastai statomas tarp verb ir particle.
Common mistakes:
❌ pick up it → ✅ pick it up.
❌ look the child after → ✅ look after the child.
Don't confuse with: Pattern yra žodyno dalis: separable arba inseparable.
Quick summary / memory hook:
separable → pick it up.
inseparable → look after it.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: B1 Phrasal verbs 3 – Exercises and explanation
Core idea: Phrasal verbs sudaro reikšmės grupes, o tas pats verb gali turėti skirtingas reikšmes su skirtingais particles.
Main rule / explanation: Lygink whole phrase ir kontekstą: take off, take up, take over – trys skirtingos konstrukcijos.
Form / structure: verb + particle = separate lexical item; meaning depends on combination.
When / why we use it: Neperkelk vieno phrasal verb reikšmės kitam su tuo pačiu verb.
Examples:
The plane took off. → Lėktuvas pakilo.
She took up a new hobby. → Ji pradėjo naują hobį.
The new manager took over the project. → Naujasis vadovas perėmė projektą.
Special cases / exceptions: Tas pats verb + kitas particle = naujas expression.
Common mistakes:
❌ take up = pakilti. → Ne: take off = pakilti.
❌ take over = pradėti hobį. → Ne: take up = pradėti užsiimti.
Don't confuse with: Kontekstas ir particle nulemia meaning.
Quick summary / memory hook:
take off = pakilti.
take up = pradėti užsiimti.
take over = perimti kontrolę.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Would rather ir would sooner reiškia pasirinkimą / pirmenybę tarp variantų.
Main rule / explanation: Would rather + V1 su tuo pačiu subject. Jei kalbame apie kito žmogaus veiksmą: I'd rather you + Past Simple. Would sooner turi panašią reikšmę ir dažnai skamba formaliau.
Form / structure: would rather + V1. would rather + person + Past Simple. would sooner + V1.
When / why we use it: Same subject: I'd rather stay. Different subject: I'd rather you came tomorrow.
Examples:
I'd rather stay. → Verčiau pasilikčiau.
I'd rather you came tomorrow. → Verčiau norėčiau, kad ateitum rytoj.
I'd sooner wait. → Verčiau palauksiu.
Special cases / exceptions: Po would rather su tuo pačiu subject nededame to.
Common mistakes:
❌ I'd rather to stay. → ✅ I'd rather stay.
❌ I'd rather you come tomorrow. → ✅ I'd rather you came tomorrow.
Don't confuse with: Same subject → rather + V1. Different subject → rather + person + Past Simple.
Quick summary / memory hook:
would rather = verčiau norėčiau.
would sooner = panaši, formalesnė konstrukcija.
Po rather → V1.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Compound adjectives with numbers: A two-day trip
Core idea: Skaičius + daiktavardis gali sudaryti compound adjective prieš kitą noun: two-day, five-minute, ten-page.
Main rule / explanation: Prieš noun toks sudėtinis apibūdinimas paprastai rašomas su hyphens, o noun compound viduje lieka singular.
Form / structure: number + singular noun + hyphens + main noun.
When / why we use it: The number+noun unit acts as one adjective before the main noun.
Examples:
We had a three-hour meeting. → Turėjome trijų valandų susitikimą.
a five-minute break. → penkių minučių pertrauka.
a ten-page report. → dešimties puslapių ataskaita.
a two-day trip. → dviejų dienų kelionė.
Special cases / exceptions: Noun compound viduje lieka singular: two-day, not two-days.
Common mistakes:
❌ a two-days trip → ✅ a two-day trip.
❌ a five-minutes break → ✅ a five-minute break.
Don't confuse with: Palygink: The trip lasted two days. / It was a two-day trip.
Quick summary / memory hook:
number + singular noun.
paprastai hyphens prieš main noun.
two-day, five-minute, ten-page.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Anglų kalbos klausimai turi skirtingas struktūras, priklausomai nuo to, kokia informacija nežinoma ir ką norime pabrėžti.
Main rule / explanation: Yes/No questions paprastai prasideda auxiliary/modal. Wh-questions prasideda question word. Jei who/what pats yra subject, do/does/did paprastai nereikia. Prielinksnis everyday English dažnai eina į pabaigą.
Form / structure: Yes/No: auxiliary/modal + subject + verb. Wh: question word + auxiliary/be + subject + verb. Subject question: Who/What + verb. Preposition: Who are you talking to?
When / why we use it: Struktūrą renkame pagal klausimo tipą ir pagal tai, kas atlieka veiksmą.
Examples:
Do you work here? → Ar dirbi čia?
Are they waiting for us? → Ar jie mūsų laukia?
Where do you work? → Kur dirbi?
Who called you? → Kas tau paskambino?
Who did you call? → Kam paskambinai?
Who are you talking to? → Su kuo kalbi?
Special cases / exceptions: Formalesnėje kalboje galima preposition prieš whom/which: To whom are you speaking? Everyday English dažniau: Who are you speaking to?
Common mistakes:
❌ Where you work? → ✅ Where do you work?
❌ Who did call you? → ✅ Who called you? (kai who = subject)
❌ What are you looking? → ✅ What are you looking for?
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia paklausk: kas nežinoma – subject, object, place, time ir t. t.? Tai padeda pasirinkti struktūrą.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Yes/No → auxiliary/modal first.
Wh-question → question word first.
Who/what as subject → usually no do/does/did.
Preposition often goes to the end.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Indirect question yra mandagesnis ir ne toks tiesioginis būdas paprašyti informacijos. Ypač naudingas darbe, aptarnavimo situacijose ir formaliuose pokalbiuose.
Main rule / explanation: Po įvadinės frazės embedded question gauna įprastą žodžių tvarką, kaip teiginyje. Yes/No klausimuose naudojami if arba whether.
Form / structure: Could you tell me + statement order? / Do you know + statement order? / ... if/whether + statement order.
When / why we use it: Direct: Where is the meeting room? Indirect: Could you tell me where the meeting room is?
Examples:
Could you tell me where the meeting room is? → Ar galėtumėte pasakyti, kur yra posėdžių kambarys?
Do you know where she works? → Ar žinote, kur ji dirba?
Could you tell me if the report is ready? → Ar galėtumėte pasakyti, ar ataskaita paruošta?
Do you know whether they have approved it? → Ar žinote, ar jie tai patvirtino?
Special cases / exceptions: Naudingos įvadinės frazės: Could you tell me...? Do you know...? Would you mind telling me...? I'd like to know...? I wonder... Pats embedded question jau yra mandagus.
Common mistakes:
❌ Do you know where does she work? → ✅ Do you know where she works?
❌ Could you tell me where is the office? → ✅ Could you tell me where the office is?
Don't confuse with: Nepainiok direct question word order ir embedded question word order.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Indirect question = polite.
Po intro → normal statement order.
Yes/No → if/whether.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Auxiliary verbs padeda sudaryti klausimus, neiginius, pabrėžimą ir įvairius laikus. Pagrindiniai auxiliaries yra be, have ir do. Modal verbs taip pat veikia kaip auxiliaries.
Main rule / explanation: BE sudaro Continuous ir Passive. HAVE sudaro Perfect. DO padeda su klausimais / neiginiais Present/Past Simple ir gali būti vartojamas pabrėžimui.
Form / structure: be + V-ing / V3. have + V3. do/does/did + V1. Modals + V1.
When / why we use it: She is working. / She has finished. / Do you understand? / I do understand your point.
Examples:
She is working. → Ji dirba.
Has she finished? → Ar ji baigė?
She doesn't understand. → Ji nesupranta.
I do understand your point. → Aš tikrai suprantu tavo mintį.
He did send the email. → Jis tikrai išsiuntė el. laišką.
Special cases / exceptions: Nedėk do, jei jau yra kitas auxiliary: Is she working? / Have they finished? Po do/does/did pagrindinis veiksmažodis lieka V1.
Common mistakes:
❌ Does she is working? → ✅ Is she working?
❌ Do they have finished? → ✅ Have they finished?
❌ Did you went? → ✅ Did you go?
Don't confuse with: Auxiliary perduoda gramatinę informaciją; main verb paprastai lieka konstrukcijai tinkamoje formoje.
Quick summary / memory hook:
be → continuous/passive.
have → perfect.
do → questions/negatives/emphasis.
modal → ability/advice/obligation + V1.
