Core idea: Konstrukcija the + comparative, the + comparative rodo, kad du pokyčiai yra susiję: kuo daugiau / mažiau keičiasi pirmasis dalykas, tuo daugiau / mažiau keičiasi antrasis.
Main rule / explanation: Abi dalys paprastai turi comparative form: the faster..., the easier... / the more..., the less... Galima vartoti adjectives ir adverbs.
Form / structure: the + comparative, the + comparative
When / why we use it: Parodome proporcingą ryšį tarp dviejų pokyčių.
Examples:
The more you practise, the more confident you become. → Kuo daugiau praktikuojiesi, tuo labiau pasitiki savimi.
The earlier we start, the sooner we can finish. → Kuo anksčiau pradėsime, tuo greičiau galėsime baigti.
The more carefully you check the data, the fewer errors you make. → Kuo atidžiau tikrini duomenis, tuo mažiau darai klaidų.
Special cases / exceptions: Tai nėra įprastas vieno daikto palyginimas su kitu. Standartiniame modelyje abi dalys prasideda the.
Common mistakes:
❌ More you learn, more you notice. → ✅ The more you learn, the more you notice.
❌ The more you practise, more confident you become. → ✅ The more you practise, the more confident you become.
Don't confuse with: Įprastas comparative: This solution is cheaper. Susijusi priklausomybė: The cheaper the solution, the more popular it becomes.
Quick summary / memory hook:
the more..., the more...
the less..., the easier...
Abi dalys – comparative.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Present Perfect Simple ir Continuous abu sieja praeitį su dabartimi, tačiau Simple dažniau rodo rezultatą / kiekį, o Continuous – trukmę ir veiklą.
Main rule / explanation: Simple = have/has + V3. Continuous = have/has been + V-ing. Stative verbs paprastai nevartojami Continuous.
Form / structure: Present Perfect Simple: have/has + V3. Present Perfect Continuous: have/has been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: I have finished the report. = rezultatas. I have been working on the report all morning. = procesas / trukmė.
Examples:
I have finished the report. → Baigiau ataskaitą.
She has visited London three times. → Ji tris kartus lankėsi Londone.
I have been working on the report all morning. → Visą rytą dirbu prie ataskaitos.
She has been studying since nine. → Ji mokosi nuo devintos.
Special cases / exceptions: Know, believe, understand, own, belong, need, want ir kai kurie kiti stative verbs paprastai nevartojami Continuous.
Common mistakes:
❌ I have been knowing her for years. → ✅ I have known her for years.
❌ She has been work since nine. → ✅ She has been working since nine.
Don't confuse with: Simple → result/achievement/number/experience. Continuous → activity/duration/recent process.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have/has + V3 = result.
have/has been + V-ing = activity/duration.
for = period; since = starting point.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Kai kurie adjectives gali būti vartojami be noun ir reikšti visą žmonių grupę: the rich, the poor, the elderly, the unemployed.
Main rule / explanation: Po the esantis adjective tokioje konstrukcijoje turi plural meaning ir žymi žmones kaip grupę. Vienam žmogui reikia įprastos noun phrase.
Form / structure: the + adjective = group of people. a/an + adjective + person/man/woman ir pan. = individual.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai norime kalbėti apie visą žmonių grupę pasitelkdami adjective + the, o ne apie vieną konkretų žmogų.
Examples:
The rich are not always happy. → Turtingieji ne visada laimingi.
The elderly often need accessible services. → Pagyvenusiems žmonėms dažnai reikia prieinamų paslaugų.
a rich person → turtingas žmogus
a/an elderly woman → pagyvenusi moteris
Special cases / exceptions: Ne kiekvieną adjective galima automatiškai paversti noun. Kai kurias tokias formas reikia mokytis kaip paruoštus patterns.
Common mistakes:
❌ The rich is not always happy. → ✅ The rich are not always happy.
❌ an unemployed (žmogui) → ✅ an unemployed man/person.
Don't confuse with: Palygink: The rich = žmonių grupė. Rich people = įprastas junginys su noun.
Quick summary / memory hook:
the + adjective → group of people.
Plural meaning → use plural verb.
Vienam žmogui reikia noun.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Kai keli adjectives apibūdina vieną noun, anglų kalba paprastai naudoja įprastą jų tvarką.
Main rule / explanation: Naudinga schema: opinion → size → age → shape → colour → origin → material → purpose → noun. Ne visos kategorijos vartojamos kartu.
Form / structure: opinion → size → age → shape → colour → origin → material → purpose → noun
When / why we use it: Naudojame natūralią tvarką, kai šalia yra du ar daugiau adjectives.
Examples:
a beautiful small old round wooden table → gražus mažas senas apvalus medinis stalas
a large modern office → didelis modernus biuras
an old French wooden chair → sena prancūziška medinė kėdė
a black leather jacket → juoda odinė striukė
Special cases / exceptions: Natūralioje kalboje dažnai pakanka 2–3 adjectives. Material ir purpose paprastai būna arčiau noun.
Common mistakes:
❌ two expensives cars → ✅ two expensive cars.
❌ Neperkelk adjective tvarkos tiesiogiai iš lietuvių kalbos.
Don't confuse with: Nereikia įsiminti milžiniškų sąrašų; svarbu suprasti kryptį nuo bendro vertinimo iki konkretesnių požymių ir material/purpose arčiau noun.
Quick summary / memory hook:
opinion → size → age → shape → colour → origin → material → purpose → noun.
Adjectives nesikeičia daugiskaitoje.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: So, such, so much, so many
Core idea: So ir such sustiprina reikšmę, tačiau reikalauja skirtingų konstrukcijų. So much ir so many rodo didelį kiekį.
Main rule / explanation: So + adjective/adverb. Such + noun phrase. So much + uncountable. So many + plural countable.
Form / structure: so + adj/adv. such + a/an + adj + singular noun. such + plural/uncountable noun. so much + uncountable. so many + plural countable.
When / why we use it: It was so difficult. / It was such a difficult task. / We had so much time. / There were so many questions.
Examples:
The service was so slow. → Aptarnavimas buvo toks lėtas.
They are such helpful people. → Tai tokie paslaugūs žmonės.
It was such an interesting idea. → Tai buvo tokia įdomi mintis.
We had so much time. → Turėjome tiek daug laiko.
There were so many customers. → Buvo tiek daug klientų.
Special cases / exceptions: Su singular countable noun: such a/an + adjective + noun. Su plural/uncountable: such + noun be a/an.
Common mistakes:
❌ so a difficult task → ✅ such a difficult task.
❌ such an expensive → ✅ such an expensive car.
❌ so many money → ✅ so much money.
Don't confuse with: Po so žiūrėk, ar eina adjective/adverb. Po such – noun phrase.
Quick summary / memory hook:
so + adjective/adverb.
such + noun phrase.
so much + uncountable.
so many + plural countable.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Narrative tenses padeda kurti istoriją: kas įvyko eilės tvarka, kas vyko tuo metu, kas įvyko anksčiau ir kiek laiko truko procesas iki praeities momento.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple – main sequence. Past Continuous – background/in progress. Past Perfect – earlier event. Past Perfect Continuous – duration/activity before a past point.
Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Kombinuok laikus, kad skaitytojui būtų aišku, kaip įvykiai susiję.
Examples:
I arrived, opened the door and sat down. → Atėjau, atidariau duris ir atsisėdau.
I was driving home when I saw the accident. → Važiavau namo, kai pamačiau avariją.
When I arrived, the meeting had already started. → Kai atvykau, susitikimas jau buvo prasidėjęs.
She was tired because she had been working all night. → Ji buvo pavargusi, nes visą naktį dirbo.
Special cases / exceptions: Past Perfect nereikia automatiškai kiekvienam „ankstesniam“ veiksmui. Jį vartok, kai svarbu parodyti ryšį su kitu praeities momentu.
Common mistakes:
❌ Every earlier action must be Past Perfect. → Ne.
❌ She had been work all night. → ✅ She had been working all night.
Don't confuse with: Galvok apie timeline: main event, background, earlier event, duration before earlier point.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple = main sequence.
Past Continuous = background.
Past Perfect = earlier.
Past Perfect Continuous = duration before past point.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Position of adverbs and adverb phrases
Core idea: Adverb vieta priklauso nuo jo tipo. Frequency, manner, time ir place phrases turi skirtingas įprastas vietas sakinyje.
Main rule / explanation: Frequency adverbs paprastai eina prieš main verb, bet po be. Manner dažnai eina po verb/object. Time/place phrases dažnai būna pabaigoje. Kai kurie adverbs gali būti perkelti į pradžią pabrėžimui.
Form / structure: frequency + main verb. be + frequency. verb/object + manner. sentence + time/place phrase.
When / why we use it: Pirmiausia nustatyk adverb funkciją, tada pasirink natūralią jo vietą.
Examples:
She usually works from home. → Ji paprastai dirba iš namų.
She is usually on time. → Ji paprastai būna laiku.
He spoke clearly. → Jis kalbėjo aiškiai.
We met in the office yesterday. → Vakar susitikome biure.
Yesterday, we discussed the problem. → Vakar aptarėme problemą.
Special cases / exceptions: Nėra taisyklės „adverb visada po verb“. Vieta priklauso nuo tipo ir struktūros.
Common mistakes:
❌ She always is late. → ✅ She is always late.
❌ He spoke the problem carefully. → Paprastai: He explained the problem carefully.
Don't confuse with: Frequency → prieš main verb, po be. Manner → dažnai po verb/object. Time/place → dažnai pabaigoje.
Quick summary / memory hook:
always/usually/often → before main verb.
With be → after be.
Manner → often after verb/object.
Time/place → often at end.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Future Continuous rodo veiksmą, kuris bus vykdomas konkrečiu ateities momentu. Future Perfect rodo, kad veiksmas bus baigtas iki ateities momento.
Main rule / explanation: Future Continuous = will be + V-ing. Future Perfect = will have + V3. Skirtumas: activity in progress vs completed before a point.
Form / structure: will be + V-ing. will have + V3.
When / why we use it: At 10 tomorrow, I will be presenting. By Friday, we will have finished the project.
Examples:
At 10 tomorrow, I will be presenting the results. → Rytoj dešimtą valandą pristatinėsiu rezultatus.
Will you be using the meeting room this afternoon? → Ar šiandien po pietų naudositės posėdžių kambariu?
By Friday, we will have finished the project. → Iki penktadienio būsime baigę projektą.
By the end of the year, she will have worked here for five years. → Iki metų pabaigos ji čia bus dirbusi penkerius metus.
Special cases / exceptions: At = konkretus momentas Future Continuous. By = deadline/latest point Future Perfect.
Common mistakes:
❌ By Friday, we will finish the report. (jei norime pabrėžti, kad iki termino bus baigta) → ✅ By Friday, we will have finished the report.
❌ will have finishing → ✅ will have finished.
Don't confuse with: At six, I will be working. = procesas šeštą. By six, I will have finished. = baigta iki šeštos.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Future Continuous → will be doing at a time.
Future Perfect → will have done by a time.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Review of all upper-intermediate verb tenses (CEFR B2.1)
Core idea: B1+ lygyje tense pasirinkimas priklauso nuo reikšmės, laiko ryšio ir kalbėtojo perspektyvos. Svarbu ne „sunkiausias laikas“, o tinkamas time + meaning relationship.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple – routine/fact/state. Present Continuous – temporary/developing. Past Simple – completed past. Past Continuous – past activity. Past Perfect – earlier past. Past Perfect Continuous – duration before past point. Present Perfect Simple/Continuous – connection/duration to now. Future forms carry different meanings.
Form / structure: Present Simple. Present Continuous. Past Simple. Past Continuous. Past Perfect. Past Perfect Continuous. Present Perfect Simple. Present Perfect Continuous. will/going to/Present Continuous/Future Continuous/Future Perfect.
When / why we use it: Naudok visą rinkinį kaip pasirinkimo sistemą, o ne kaip atskirų formulių sąrašą.
Examples:
I usually work from home. → Paprastai dirbu iš namų.
I'm working on a new process this week. → Šią savaitę dirbu prie naujo proceso.
I was checking the data when she called. → Tikrinau duomenis, kai ji paskambino.
I had finished before the meeting. → Buvau baigęs prieš susitikimą.
I've been working all morning. → Visą rytą dirbu.
By Friday, I'll have finished. → Iki penktadienio būsiu baigęs.
Special cases / exceptions: Viena time expression ne visada automatiškai parenka tense. Pirmiausia žiūrėk į meaning ir perspective.
Common mistakes:
❌ Rinktis tense tik pagal today/yesterday/next week.
✅ Pirmiausia nustatyti: routine, process, result, duration, earlier event, arrangement, deadline ir t. t.
Don't confuse with: Pagrindinis klausimas: „Kokį laiko ryšį noriu parodyti?“
Quick summary / memory hook: Ne „kuris laikas sudėtingesnis“, o „kokį time + meaning relationship noriu parodyti?“
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Used to, be used to, get used to
Core idea: Used to, be used to ir get used to apibūdina tris skirtingas idėjas: praeities įprotį, dabartinį pripratimą ir pripratimo procesą.
Main rule / explanation: Used to + V1 = praeities įprotis / būsena, kurios dabar nebėra. Be used to + noun/-ing = būti pripratusiam. Get used to + noun/-ing = priprasti.
Form / structure: used to + V1. be used to + noun/V-ing. get used to + noun/V-ing.
When / why we use it: Pirmiausia nustatyk: kalbama apie praeitį, dabartinį pripratimą ar pripratimo procesą.
Examples:
I used to work there. → Anksčiau ten dirbau.
We used to live in the city. → Anksčiau gyvenome mieste.
I am used to working late. → Esu pripratęs dirbti iki vėlumos.
You will get used to working with the new system. → Priprasi dirbti su naująja sistema.
Special cases / exceptions: Be/get used to žodis to yra preposition, todėl po jo veiksmažodis gauna -ing: I am used to getting up early.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am used to get up early. → ✅ I am used to getting up early.
❌ I used to working there. → ✅ I used to work there.
Don't confuse with: Used to drive = anksčiau vairavau. Be used to driving = dabar esu pripratęs vairuoti.
Quick summary / memory hook:
used to + V1 = past habit/state.
be used to + noun/-ing = familiar now.
get used to + noun/-ing = become familiar.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Would and used to – past habits and repeated actions
Core idea: Used to ir would gali apibūdinti pasikartojančius veiksmus praeityje, tačiau used to taip pat gali apibūdinti praeities būsenas.
Main rule / explanation: Would gerai tinka pasakojimuose apie repeated past actions. Used to tinka ir repeated actions, ir past states.
Form / structure: used to + V1. would + V1 repeated past action.
When / why we use it: Pasikartojantis veiksmas: When I was a child, I would visit my grandparents every weekend. Praeities būsena: I used to live in Kyiv.
Examples:
When I was a child, I used to visit my grandparents every weekend. → Kai buvau vaikas, kiekvieną savaitgalį lankydavau senelius.
When I was a child, I would visit my grandparents every weekend. → Kai buvau vaikas, kiekvieną savaitgalį lankydavau senelius.
I used to live in Kyiv. → Anksčiau gyvenau Kyjive.
Special cases / exceptions: Would paprastai nevartojamas praeities būsenoms: live, be, know ir kt. Vienam atskiram įvykiui netinka nei used to, nei would.
Common mistakes:
❌ I would live in Kyiv when I was a child. → ✅ I used to live in Kyiv.
❌ I would visit them last Sunday. → ✅ I visited them last Sunday.
Don't confuse with: Would čia nereiškia tiesiog „būsiu“ ar conditional. Šioje pamokoje jis reiškia būdingą pasikartojantį veiksmą praeityje.
Quick summary / memory hook:
used to = repeated action + past state.
would = repeated past action.
Single event → Past Simple.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Gerund ir infinitive yra skirtingi verb patterns. Kai kuriems verbs reikia -ing, kai kuriems to + V1, o kai kurie leidžia abi formas, kartais pakeisdami reikšmę.
Main rule / explanation: Gerund patterns: avoid/enjoy/suggest/finish + V-ing. Infinitive patterns: decide/hope/plan/want + to + V1. Kai kurie verbs turi du modelius.
Form / structure: verb + V-ing. verb + to + V1. Some verbs + both.
When / why we use it: Forma po pirmojo verb yra jo grammar pattern dalis.
Examples:
I enjoy reading. → Man patinka skaityti.
We decided to leave. → Nusprendėme išeiti.
She suggested taking a taxi. → Ji pasiūlė važiuoti taksi.
I stopped smoking. → Nustojau rūkyti.
I stopped to smoke. → Sustojau parūkyti.
Special cases / exceptions: Po preposition vartojame -ing: interested in learning, thank you for helping.
Common mistakes:
❌ I enjoy to work here. → ✅ I enjoy working here.
❌ She suggested to take a taxi. → ✅ She suggested taking a taxi.
❌ interested in to learn → ✅ interested in learning.
Don't confuse with: Žiūrėk ne tik į verb vertimą, o į tai, kokios formos jis reikalauja ir ar forma keičia meaning.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Verb pattern = žodyno vieneto dalis.
preposition → V-ing.
enjoy/suggest/finish → V-ing.
decide/hope/plan/want → to + V1.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Past modal deduction padeda daryti išvadą apie tai, kas tikriausiai įvyko praeityje.
Main rule / explanation: Must have + V3 = stipri išvada. May/might/could have + V3 = galimas paaiškinimas. Can't have + V3 = stipri išvada, kad tai neįmanoma / neįvyko.
Form / structure: must have + V3. may/might/could have + V3. can't have + V3.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai žiūrime į evidence ir darome išvadą apie praeitį, o ne kalbame apie permission/ability.
Examples:
They must have forgotten the meeting. → Turbūt jie pamiršo susitikimą.
She might have missed the bus. → Galbūt ji nespėjo į autobusą.
He could have misunderstood the message. → Galbūt jis neteisingai suprato žinutę.
They can't have finished already. → Negali būti, kad jie jau baigė.
Special cases / exceptions: Must have čia reiškia deduction, o ne obligation. Po have reikia V3.
Common mistakes:
❌ She might has left. → ✅ She might have left.
❌ He must go = past deduction. → Ne, tai obligation; past deduction: He must have gone.
Don't confuse with: Palygink must go = privalo eiti ir must have gone = turbūt išėjo.
Quick summary / memory hook:
must have + V3 = strong deduction.
might/could have + V3 = possibility.
can't have + V3 = strong impossibility.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Likely, unlikely, bound, definitely, probably – probability
Core idea: Anglų kalboje tikimybei išreikšti yra keli būdai: probably, definitely, likely, unlikely ir be bound to.
Main rule / explanation: Probably = tikriausiai. Definitely = tikrai / neabejotinai. Likely/unlikely = tikėtina / mažai tikėtina. Be bound to = beveik neabejotinai / labai tikėtina.
Form / structure: will probably + V1. be probably + place/adjective. definitely + clause. be likely/unlikely to + V1. be bound to + V1.
When / why we use it: Dėk adverb į natūralią vietą ir rinkis konstrukciją pagal reikšmę.
Examples:
She will probably arrive soon. → Ji tikriausiai greitai atvyks.
He is probably at home. → Jis tikriausiai yra namuose.
We will definitely need more time. → Mums tikrai reikės daugiau laiko.
It is likely to rain. → Tikėtina, kad lis.
They are unlikely to agree. → Mažai tikėtina, kad jie sutiks.
The new system is bound to create questions. → Naujoji sistema beveik neabejotinai sukels klausimų.
Special cases / exceptions: Likely galimas dviem modeliais: It is likely that prices will rise. / Prices are likely to rise. Pretty flexible stiprumas priklauso nuo context; čia kalbame būtent apie probability.
Common mistakes:
❌ She will probably comes. → ✅ She will probably come.
❌ They are likely agree. → ✅ They are likely to agree.
Don't confuse with: Probably/definitely – adverbs. Likely/unlikely/bound to – adjective-based structures.
Quick summary / memory hook:
probably = tikriausiai.
definitely = tikrai.
likely = tikėtina.
unlikely = mažai tikėtina.
bound to = labai tikėtina / tikėtina, kad būtinai.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Would rather ir would prefer abu reiškia preference, tačiau po jų vartojamos skirtingos struktūros.
Main rule / explanation: Would rather + V1. Kito žmogaus veiksmui: I'd rather you + Past Simple. Would prefer + noun arba to-infinitive.
Form / structure: would rather + V1. would rather + person + Past Simple. would prefer + noun / to + V1. rather than + base/infinitive pattern in comparison.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai lyginame du galimus pasirinkimus ir sakome, kuriam teikiame pirmenybę.
Examples:
I'd rather stay. → Verčiau pasilikčiau.
I'd rather you came tomorrow. → Verčiau norėčiau, kad ateitum rytoj.
I'd prefer tea. → Verčiau rinkčiausi arbatą.
I'd prefer to stay home. → Verčiau likčiau namuose.
I'd prefer to work from home rather than travel. → Verčiau dirbčiau iš namų, o ne važinėčiau.
Special cases / exceptions: Po would rather su tuo pačiu subject nededame to. Past form po you preference konstrukcijoje nebūtinai reiškia praeitį.
Common mistakes:
❌ I'd rather to stay. → ✅ I'd rather stay.
❌ I'd prefer stay. → ✅ I'd prefer to stay.
Don't confuse with: rather + V1. prefer + noun/to-infinitive.
Quick summary / memory hook:
would rather + V1.
would prefer + noun/to + V1.
Different subject after rather → Past Simple.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Verbs of the senses: look, sound, feel, etc.
Core idea: Look, sound, smell, taste ir feel gali apibūdinti, kokį įspūdį kažkas sukelia mūsų pojūčiams. Tokia reikšme po jų dažnai eina adjective.
Main rule / explanation: Po sense verb dažnai vartojamas adjective: look tired, sound interesting, smell great, taste strange, feel soft. Like įveda comparison.
Form / structure: subject + sense verb + adjective. sense verb + like + noun.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai apibūdiname įspūdį, kurį objektas daro pojūčiams, arba lyginame jį su kažkuo.
Examples:
You look tired. → Atrodai pavargęs.
That sounds interesting. → Tai skamba įdomiai.
The food smells great. → Maistas puikiai kvepia.
This tastes strange. → Skonis keistas.
The fabric feels soft. → Audinys švelnus liečiant.
Special cases / exceptions: Nepainiok look = seem/appearance su look at = nukreipti žvilgsnį. Soup tastes good, o ne tastes well, kai kalbame apie flavour.
Common mistakes:
❌ The soup tastes well. → ✅ The soup tastes good.
❌ She looks at tired. → ✅ She looks tired.
Don't confuse with: Sense verb + adjective apibūdina subject. Sense verb + like įveda comparison: It looks like rain.
Quick summary / memory hook:
look/sound/smell/taste/feel + adjective.
+ like + noun for comparison.
look at ≠ look.

Core idea: Passive Voice galima sudaryti beveik bet kuriame pagrindiniame tense. Pagrindinis raktas išlieka tas pats: be + V3.
Main rule / explanation: Keičiasi be forma, o pagrindinis lexical verb lieka V3: is checked, was sent, is being tested, has been fixed, will be fixed, must be reported.
Form / structure: Present Simple: am/is/are + V3. Past Simple: was/were + V3. Present Continuous: am/is/are being + V3. Past Continuous: was/were being + V3. Present Perfect: has/have been + V3. Past Perfect: had been + V3. Future: will be + V3. Modal: modal + be + V3.
When / why we use it: Passive tense rinkis pagal veiksmo laiką, išlaikydamas be + V3.
Examples:
The reports are checked every morning. → Ataskaitos tikrinamos kiekvieną rytą.
The system is being tested. → Sistema dabar testuojama.
The problem has been fixed. → Problema jau ištaisyta.
The problem had been fixed before the meeting. → Problema buvo ištaisyta prieš susitikimą.
The issue must be reported. → Apie problemą reikia pranešti.
Special cases / exceptions: by + agent dedame, jei performer svarbus: The software was developed by a small team. Jei performer unknown/obvious/unimportant, jo praleidžiame.
Common mistakes:
❌ The system is test. → ✅ The system is being tested.
❌ The problem will fixed. → ✅ The problem will be fixed.
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia nustatyk tense, tada parink be formą ir V3.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Passive core = be + V3.
Tense yra be.
Modal passive = modal + be + V3.

Lesson / Topic: Zero and first conditional and future time clauses
Core idea: Zero Conditional apibūdina bendras tiesas, taisykles, routines ir nuspėjamus rezultatus. First Conditional – realią galimybę ateityje.
Main rule / explanation: Zero: if/when + Present Simple, Present Simple. First: if + Present Simple, will + V1. Future time clauses su when/as soon as/before/after/until/once vartoja Present, o ne will.
Form / structure: Zero: If + Present, Present. First: If + Present, will + V1. Time clause: when/as soon as/etc. + Present.
When / why we use it: Naudojame general truths/predictable results ir realistic future conditions/time sequences.
Examples:
If you heat ice, it melts. → Jei pašildai ledą, jis ištirpsta.
When the system detects an error, it sends an alert. → Kai sistema aptinka klaidą, ji siunčia alert.
If it rains, we will stay inside. → Jei lis, liksime viduje.
As soon as she arrives, we'll start. → Kai tik ji atvyks, pradėsime.
Special cases / exceptions: Future time clause will paprastai nevartojamas: When I finish, I will call you. Result clause gali turėti will, modal arba imperative.
Common mistakes:
❌ When I will finish, I will call you. → ✅ When I finish, I will call you.
❌ If you heat ice, it will melt. → General truth atveju standartiškiau If you heat ice, it melts.
Don't confuse with: Zero = general/predictable result. First = realistic future possibility.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Zero: Present → Present.
First: Present → will.
Future time clause → Present, not will.

Lesson / Topic: Second and third conditionals – unreal conditionals
Core idea: Second Conditional rodo unreal/hypothetical present or future. Third Conditional – unreal past ir įsivaizduojamą jo rezultatą.
Main rule / explanation: Second: if + Past Simple, would + V1. Third: if + Past Perfect, would have + V3. Could/might gali pakeisti would, kai reikia ability/possibility reikšmės.
Form / structure: Second: If + V2, would + V1. Third: If + had + V3, would have + V3.
When / why we use it: Naudojame hypothetical/unreal situations: Second – now/future, Third – past.
Examples:
If I had more time, I would learn another language. → Jei turėčiau daugiau laiko, mokyčiausi kitos kalbos.
If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train. → Jei būtume išėję anksčiau, būtume spėję į traukinį.
If I had more time, I could help. → Jei turėčiau daugiau laiko, galėčiau padėti.
Special cases / exceptions: If-clause nenaudok would: If I had known..., ne If I would have known.... Past forma Second nebūtinai rodo praeitį.
Common mistakes:
❌ If I would have known... → ✅ If I had known...
❌ If I had more time, I would have helped yesterday. → Third Conditional: If I had had more time, I would have helped.
Don't confuse with: Žiūrėk į time: unreal now/future → Second; unreal past → Third.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Second → if + Past, would + V1.
Third → if + Past Perfect, would have + V3.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Wishes and regrets – I wish / if only
Core idea: I wish ir if only parodo, kad norime, jog situacija būtų kitokia. Forma priklauso nuo to, ar kalbame apie dabartį, praeitį, ar erzinančią situaciją.
Main rule / explanation: Present wish: wish + Past Simple. Past regret: wish + Past Perfect. Annoying situation/change in behaviour: wish + would.
Form / structure: wish + V2. wish + had + V3. wish + would + V1.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai norime, kad dabartis būtų kitokia, išreiškiame apgailestavimą dėl praeities arba norime pakeisti elgesį / situaciją.
Examples:
I wish I knew the answer. → Norėčiau, kad žinočiau atsakymą.
If only I had more time. → Jei tik turėčiau daugiau laiko.
I wish I had studied harder. → Gaila, kad nesimokiau daugiau.
I wish you would stop interrupting. → Norėčiau, kad nustotum pertraukinėti.
Special cases / exceptions: Wish + would paprastai susijęs su kito žmogaus elgesiu arba situacija, kurią kalbėtojas nori pakeisti. Nerealios dabarties atveju negalima tiesiog vartoti Present Simple.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish I know the answer. → ✅ I wish I knew the answer.
❌ I wish I had more time yesterday. → Past regret: I wish I had had more time.
Don't confuse with: Present unreal → Past Simple. Past regret → Past Perfect. Want behaviour/situation to change → would.
Quick summary / memory hook:
wish + Past = noriu, kad dabartis būtų kitokia.
wish + had + V3 = apgailestavimas dėl praeities.
wish + would = noriu pokyčio.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Participles -ing ir -ed gali veikti kaip adjectives. Pagrindinis skirtumas: priežastis / poveikis arba žmogaus jausmas / būsena.
Main rule / explanation: -ing paprastai apibūdina tai, kas sukelia jausmą arba turi tam tikrą effect. -ed paprastai apibūdina, ką žmogus jaučia / patiria.
Form / structure: -ing adjective: boring, confusing, interesting. -ed adjective: bored, confused, interested.
When / why we use it: Naudojame participles kaip adjectives, kai norime apibūdinti jausmo šaltinį / poveikį arba žmogaus patirtį.
Examples:
The film was boring. → Filmas buvo nuobodus.
I was bored. → Man buvo nuobodu.
The instructions were confusing. → Instrukcijos buvo painios.
I was confused by the instructions. → Instrukcijos mane supainiojo.
The news was shocking. → Naujienos buvo šokiruojančios.
We were shocked. → Buvome sukrėsti.
Special cases / exceptions: Nesirink -ed automatiškai vien todėl, kad subject yra žmogus. Pirmiausia paklausk: feeling/experience ar cause/source?
Common mistakes:
❌ The news was shocked. → ✅ The news was shocking.
❌ I was confusing. → ✅ I was confused.
Don't confuse with: -ing = source/cause/effect. -ed = experience/feeling.
Quick summary / memory hook:
-ing → sukelia jausmą.
-ed → jaučia / patiria.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Passive with reporting verbs leidžia pateikti informaciją, kai šaltinis yra bendras, nežinomas arba nesvarbus.
Main rule / explanation: Dvi pagrindinės schemos: It is said/believed/expected that... ir person/thing + is said/believed/expected + to-infinitive. Infinitive laikas rodo relationship.
Form / structure: It is + V3 reporting verb + that-clause. Subject + is/are + V3 reporting verb + to + V1 / to have + V3.
When / why we use it: It is believed that the company will expand. / The company is believed to be expanding. / He is believed to have left.
Examples:
It is believed that the company will expand. → Manoma, kad įmonė plėsis.
The company is believed to be expanding. → Manoma, kad įmonė plečiasi.
The CEO is expected to announce the decision soon. → Tikimasi, kad CEO netrukus paskelbs sprendimą.
He is believed to have left the country. → Manoma, kad jis išvyko iš šalies.
Special cases / exceptions: Simple infinitive gali apibūdinti dabartinę situaciją; perfect infinitive to have + V3 rodo ankstesnį veiksmą.
Common mistakes:
❌ He is believed to has stolen the money. → ✅ He is believed to have stolen the money.
❌ The company is said expanding. → ✅ The company is said to be expanding.
Don't confuse with: Žiūrėk, kur yra focus: general source → It is said that...; person/thing → is said to...
Quick summary / memory hook:
It is said/believed/expected that...
Subject is said/believed/expected to + V1/be + V-ing/to have + V3.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Have something done reiškia, kad tu suorganizavai paslaugą, o veiksmą atliko kitas žmogus.
Main rule / explanation: Pattern: have + object + V3. Tense keičiasi pagal have formą. Konstrukcija taip pat gali apibūdinti nepageidaujamą įvykį, nutikusį žmogui.
Form / structure: have + object + V3. I had my car repaired. I am having my hair cut. I will have my laptop repaired.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai darbo neatliekame patys, o organizuojame, kad jį atliktų kitas žmogus.
Examples:
I had my car repaired. → Atidaviau automobilį remontuoti / man sutvarkė automobilį.
She is having her hair cut. → Jai dabar kerpa plaukus.
We had the office cleaned. → Užsakėme biuro valymą.
He had his phone stolen. → Iš jo pavogė telefoną.
Special cases / exceptions: Kontekstas rodo, ar paslauga buvo užsakyta, ar žmogų ištiko nemalonus įvykis.
Common mistakes:
❌ I repaired my car. = someone else did it for me. → Ne: tai reiškia, kad automobilį remontavau pats.
✅ I had my car repaired. = remontą atliko kitas žmogus.
Don't confuse with: Active: I repaired my car. Causative: I had my car repaired.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have + object + V3 = suorganizavau veiksmą objektui.
Tense keičiasi have.
Gali reikšti ir nemalonų įvykį.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Reporting verbs perduoda ne tik kalbėjimo faktą, bet ir žinutės būdą / tikslą: agree, promise, admit, deny, suggest, advise ir kiti turi skirtingus patterns.
Main rule / explanation: Skirtingiems verbs reikia skirtingų konstrukcijų: verb + to-infinitive, verb + -ing, verb + object + to-infinitive arba that-clause.
Form / structure: Verb + to: agree/promise/refuse/offer + to V1. Verb + -ing: admit/deny/suggest/recommend + V-ing. Verb + object + to: advise/encourage/remind/warn + object + to V1. Some + that-clause.
When / why we use it: Mokykis reporting verb kartu su pattern, o ne atskirai.
Examples:
She agreed to help. → Ji sutiko padėti.
He admitted making a mistake. → Jis pripažino padaręs klaidą.
They suggested taking a taxi. → Jie pasiūlė važiuoti taksi.
She advised me to wait. → Ji patarė man palaukti.
He explained that the plan had changed. → Jis paaiškino, kad planas pasikeitė.
Special cases / exceptions: Suggest ypač svarbus: standard pattern yra suggest + V-ing: She suggested taking a taxi.
Common mistakes:
❌ She suggested to take a taxi. → ✅ She suggested taking a taxi.
❌ He advised to wait. → ✅ He advised me to wait. (šioje konstrukcijoje reikia object)
Don't confuse with: Veiksmažodžio reikšmė ne visada nurodo jo grammar pattern. Pattern reikia mokytis kartu su verb.
Quick summary / memory hook:
agree/promise/refuse/offer + to.
admit/deny/suggest/recommend + -ing.
advice/encourage/remind/warn + object + to.
explain/claim/admit + that-clause.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Clauses of contrast rodo netikėtą skirtumą. Purpose clauses paaiškina tikslą: kodėl / kokiu tikslu kažką darome.
Main rule / explanation: Although/even though/whereas/while įveda contrast. To + V1, in order to, so as to + V1 reiškia purpose. So that + clause. Despite/in spite of paprastai + noun/V-ing.
Form / structure: although/even though/whereas/while + clause. to/in order to/so as to + V1. so that + clause. despite/in spite of + noun/V-ing.
When / why we use it: Konstrukciją rinkis pagal idėją: contrast, purpose arba negative purpose.
Examples:
Although it was expensive, we bought it. → Nors tai buvo brangu, nusipirkome.
Whereas the first option is cheap, the second is faster. → Pirmasis variantas pigus, o antrasis greitesnis.
I called to confirm the booking. → Paskambinau, kad patvirtinčiau rezervaciją.
We checked the address so as not to make a mistake. → Patikrinome adresą, kad nepadarytume klaidos.
I wrote it down so that I wouldn't forget. → Užsirašiau, kad nepamirščiau.
Special cases / exceptions: Although/even though reikalauja clause. Despite/in spite of paprastai eina prieš noun arba -ing: Despite being tired...
Common mistakes:
❌ Although it was late, but we continued. → But nereikia.
❌ Despite it was late... → ✅ Although it was late... / Despite being tired...
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia nuspręsk: unexpected contrast? → although/whereas. goal? → to/in order to/so that. noun/-ing after despite.
Quick summary / memory hook:
contrast → although/even though/whereas/while.
purpose → to/in order to/so as to/so that.
despite/in spite of + noun/-ing.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Whatever, whenever, wherever, whoever ir however gali pradėti clauses su atvira / neribota reikšme: bet koks objektas, žmogus, vieta ar laikas.
Main rule / explanation: Whatever = anything that. Whoever = any person who. Wherever = any place where. Whenever = any time that. However + adjective/adverb = no matter how.
Form / structure: whatever/whoever/wherever/whenever + clause. however + adjective/adverb + clause.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai konkretus variantas nesvarbus arba reikšmė yra „nesvarbu koks / kas / kur / kada / kiek“.
Examples:
Take whatever you need. → Imk viską, ko tau reikia.
Whoever finishes first can leave. → Kas pirmas baigs, gali išeiti.
We can meet wherever you prefer. → Galime susitikti bet kur, kur tau patogu.
Call me whenever you need help. → Skambink man, kai tik tau reikės pagalbos.
However difficult it is, we will continue. → Kad ir kaip būtų sunku, tęsime.
Special cases / exceptions: However čia gali reikšti „kad ir kaip / nepriklausomai nuo to, kiek“. Nepainiok su however = „tačiau“.
Common mistakes:
❌ However alone in However difficult it is... = „tačiau“. → Čia however = no matter how.
❌ Wherever + noun only. → Toliau turi būti clause / location idea.
Don't confuse with: However difficult = no matter how difficult. However alone as linking adverb = but/nevertheless.
Quick summary / memory hook:
whatever = anything that.
whoever = any person who.
wherever = any place where.
whenever = any time.
however + adj/adv = no matter how.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Quantifiers – all, most, both, either, neither, any, no, none
Core idea: Šie quantifiers padeda kalbėti apie visą kiekį, daugumą, du variantus, vieną iš dviejų, nė vieną iš dviejų ir neapibrėžtą pasirinkimą.
Main rule / explanation: All = whole group. Most = majority. Both = two together. Either = one of two. Neither = not one/not the other. Any priklauso nuo konteksto. No + noun. None stovi savarankiškai.
Form / structure: all + noun. most + noun / most of + determiner. both + plural / both of. either/neither + singular or of + plural pronoun. no + noun. none without noun.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai reikia palyginti visos grupės kiekį, daugumą ar pasirinkimo variantus.
Examples:
All the employees attended. → Visi darbuotojai dalyvavo.
Most people agreed. → Dauguma žmonių sutiko.
Both options are possible. → Abu variantai galimi.
Either option is acceptable. → Tinka bet kuris iš dviejų variantų.
Neither option works. → Nė vienas iš dviejų variantų netinka.
You can choose any option. → Gali pasirinkti bet kurį variantą.
No employees were available. → Nebuvo nė vieno darbuotojo.
None of the employees were available. → Nė vieno darbuotojo nebuvo.
Special cases / exceptions: None nestatomas tiesiai prieš noun: none of the students, bet no students. Most of + specific group naudoja determiner.
Common mistakes:
❌ none students → ✅ no students / none of the students.
❌ Both of three options → ✅ Both of the two options / all three options.
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia suskaičiuok grupę ir nuspręsk, ar reikia konkrečios grupės.
Quick summary / memory hook:
all = whole.
most = majority.
both = 2 together.
either = 1 of 2.
neither = 0 of 2.
no + noun.
none = pronoun.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Standartinėje anglų kalboje clause paprastai turi vieną neigiamą elementą. Anything/anyone/anywhere ir ever padeda sudaryti neiginį be antro negative.
Main rule / explanation: Po not dažnai vartojami anything, anyone, anywhere, ever. Nobody/nothing/nowhere jau turi neigiamą reikšmę ir paprastai nereikalauja not.
Form / structure: not + any/ever forms. arba positive clause + no/nobody/nothing/nowhere.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai norime sudaryti neigiamą sakinį standartiniu būdu be dviejų negative elements.
Examples:
I don't know anything. → Aš nieko nežinau.
She didn't see anyone. → Ji nieko / nieko žmogaus nematė.
We haven't been anywhere. → Mes niekur nebuvome.
I know nothing. → Aš nieko nežinau.
Nobody called. → Niekas nepaskambino.
Special cases / exceptions: Kai kuriuose non-standard varieties pasitaiko double negatives, bet standard formal English jų paprastai vengiama.
Common mistakes:
❌ I don't know nothing. → ✅ I don't know anything. / I know nothing.
❌ Nobody didn't call. → ✅ Nobody called.
❌ I don't hardly know him. → ✅ I hardly know him.
Don't confuse with: Jei žodis jau yra negative (nothing, nobody, nowhere, rarely/hardly), nedėk papildomo not be specialios priežasties.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Standard English → one negative element.
not + anything/anyone/anywhere.
nothing/nobody/nowhere already negative.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Already, still, yet – What's the difference?
Core idea: Already, still ir yet parodo skirtingą santykį su tikėtinu laiku: jau įvyko, vis dar tęsiasi arba dar neįvyko.
Main rule / explanation: Already = sooner than expected/before now. Still = situation continues. Yet = expected event has not happened, dažniausiai klausimuose / neiginiuose.
Form / structure: have + already + V3. still + main verb / after be. yet often at end.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai norime parodyti: veiksmas jau įvyko, situacija tęsiasi arba laukiamas įvykis dar neįvyko.
Examples:
I've already finished. → Jau baigiau.
Is she already here? → Ar ji jau čia?
I still work there. → Aš vis dar ten dirbu.
She is still working. → Ji vis dar dirba.
Have you finished yet? → Ar jau baigei?
I haven't finished yet. → Dar nebaigiau.
Special cases / exceptions: Position is part of the pattern: already dažnai tarp auxiliary ir main verb; still prieš main verb, bet po be; yet dažnai pabaigoje.
Common mistakes:
❌ I yet haven't finished. → Neutral: I haven't finished yet.
❌ I yet live here. → ✅ I still live here.
Don't confuse with: Still = tęsiasi. Yet = laukiamas pokytis dar neįvyko. Already = įvyko anksčiau / iki dabar.
Quick summary / memory hook:
already = jau.
still = vis dar.
yet = dar / jau? klausimuose ir neiginiuose.
Position matters.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Needn't, don't need to, didn't need to, needn't have
Core idea: Needn't, don't need to, didn't need to ir needn't have panašūs, tačiau apibūdina skirtingas būtinybės situacijas.
Main rule / explanation: Don't need to / needn't = nėra būtinybės dabar. Didn't need to = nebuvo būtinybės praeityje; savaime nenurodo, ar veiksmas įvyko. Needn't have + V3 = veiksmas įvyko, bet buvo nereikalingas.
Form / structure: don't need to + V1. needn't + V1. didn't need to + V1. needn't have + V3.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai reikia tiksliai atskirti dabartinį / praeities nebūtinumą ir jau atliktą nereikalingą veiksmą.
Examples:
You don't need to come early. → Tau nereikia ateiti anksti.
You needn't wait. → Tau nereikia laukti.
We didn't need to book a room. → Mums nereikėjo rezervuoti kambario.
You needn't have bought so much food. → Nereikėjo pirkti tiek daug maisto (bet tu nupirkai).
Special cases / exceptions: Pagrindinis skirtumas: didn't need to nepasako, ar žmogus atliko veiksmą; needn't have aiškiai rodo, kad veiksmas buvo atliktas ir buvo nereikalingas.
Common mistakes:
❌ We didn't need to buy food = būtinai nupirkome. → Ne, tai nepasakyta.
❌ You needn't have bought food = nepirkai. → Ne, pirkai, bet veltui.
Don't confuse with: Žiūrėk į outcome: veiksmas įvyko? Jei taip ir buvo unnecessary → needn't have + V3.
Quick summary / memory hook:
don't need to / needn't = no necessity now.
didn't need to = no past necessity; outcome unspecified.
needn't have + V3 = done, but unnecessary.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Pretty, Rather, Quite, Fairly – Adverbs of degree
Core idea: Pretty, rather, quite ir fairly yra adverbs of degree. Jie stiprina adjective/adverb, tačiau jų stiprumas ir atspalvis priklauso nuo konteksto.
Main rule / explanation: Fairly dažnai reiškia moderately. Pretty – šnekamasis „gana“. Rather gali reikšti quite ir kartais suteikia stipresnį / netikėtą ar nepageidaujamą atspalvį. Quite priklauso nuo adjective ir context.
Form / structure: fairly + adj. pretty + adj. rather + adj. quite + adj/adv.
When / why we use it: Rinkis ne pagal matematinę skalę, o pagal kontekstą, tone ir adjective.
Examples:
The task was fairly easy. → Užduotis buvo gana lengva.
The task was pretty difficult. → Užduotis buvo gana sudėtinga.
It's rather expensive. → Tai gana brangu.
The room is quite large. → Kambarys gana didelis.
quite impossible / quite certain → visiškai neįmanoma / visiškai užtikrinta.
Special cases / exceptions: Quite gali suteikti skirtingą stiprumą su skirtingais adjectives. Šie žodžiai lankstūs, o intonation/context keičia atspalvį.
Common mistakes: ❌ Laikyti fairly = tiksliai 50 %, pretty = tiksliai 70 % ir pan. → Ne, tikslios matematinės skalės nėra.
Don't confuse with: Tai degree adverbs, bet jų exact strength depends on context and adjective.
Quick summary / memory hook:
fairly = vidutiniškai.
pretty = informal quite.
rather = quite, kartais netikėta / nepageidaujama.
quite = flexible, context-dependent.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: When I do vs When I have done – Future time clauses
Core idea: Future time clauses po when, once, as soon as, after, before ir until paprastai vartoja Present, tačiau kartais reikia Present Perfect, kad pabrėžtume pirmo veiksmo užbaigimą.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple rodo įprastą būsimų įvykių seką. Present Perfect pabrėžia, kad pirmasis veiksmas bus visiškai baigtas prieš antrąjį.
Form / structure: When I finish the report, I'll send it. / When I have finished the report, I'll send it.
When / why we use it: Use Present Simple neutraliai sequence. Use Present Perfect, kai completion svarbus. Main clause gali turėti will.
Examples:
When I finish the report, I'll send it. → Kai baigsiu ataskaitą, ją išsiųsiu.
When I have finished the report, I'll send it. → Kai jau būsiu baigęs ataskaitą, ją išsiųsiu.
As soon as we have received the data, we will start the analysis. → Kai tik gausime duomenis, pradėsime analizę.
Special cases / exceptions: Nedėk will į standard future time clause: When I will finish... yra neteisinga. Present form gauna future meaning dėl connector.
Common mistakes:
❌ When I will finish, I'll send it. → ✅ When I finish, I'll send it.
❌ When I have finish... → ✅ When I have finished...
Don't confuse with: finish = neutrali sequence. have finished = pabrėžtas completion before next event.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Future time clause → Present, not will.
Present Simple = sequence.
Present Perfect = completion emphasized.

Lesson / Topic: Do or Make – Which is it?
Core idea: Do ir make abu gali būti verčiami „daryti“, tačiau anglų kalboje pasirenkami pagal pastovų junginį.
Main rule / explanation: Do dažnai vartojamas su activities, tasks, work ir actions. Make – su creating, producing, preparing arba causing something. Daug junginių reikia mokytis kaip collocations.
Form / structure: do + collocation. make + collocation.
When / why we use it: Mokykis dažnų junginių, o ne bandyk lietuvišką veiksmažodį „daryti“ versti tiesiogiai.
Examples:
do homework. → daryti namų darbus.
do research. → atlikti tyrimą.
do exercise. → daryti pratimus.
do your best. → stengtis iš visų jėgų.
make a decision. → priimti sprendimą.
make a mistake. → padaryti klaidą.
make a plan. → sudaryti planą.
make money. → uždirbti pinigų.
make an appointment. → susitarti dėl susitikimo.
make progress. → daryti pažangą.
do someone a favour. → padaryti paslaugą.
do damage. → padaryti žalą.
Special cases / exceptions: Yra exceptions, todėl saugiausia dažnus junginius mokytis kaip collocations.
Common mistakes:
❌ do a decision → ✅ make a decision.
❌ make homework → ✅ do homework.
❌ make a research → ✅ do research.
Don't confuse with: Neversti „daryti“ žodis į žodį. Pirmiausia prisimink collocation.
Quick summary / memory hook:
do = activities/tasks/work/actions.
make = create/produce/prepare/result.
Svarbiausia – collocations.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Have gali būti įprastas pagrindinis veiksmažodis arba pagalbinis veiksmažodis. Vaidmenį lemia visa konstrukcija.
Main rule / explanation: Kaip main verb have reiškia turėjimą, patirtį ar dalyvavimą: I have a car. Kaip auxiliary, have sudaro Perfect: I have finished.
Form / structure: Main verb: have + noun. Questions/negatives: do/does/did + have. Auxiliary: have/has/had + V3.
When / why we use it: Do you have a minute? / I don't have enough information. / I have finished the report. / She had already left.
Examples:
I have a car. → Turiu automobilį.
She has breakfast at seven. → Ji pusryčiauja septintą.
Do you have a minute? → Ar turite minutėlę?
I don't have enough information. → Neturiu pakankamai informacijos.
I have solved the problem. → Išsprendžiau problemą.
They will have completed the work by Friday. → Iki penktadienio jie bus baigę darbą.
Special cases / exceptions: Kai have jau yra auxiliary Perfect, do nereikia: Have you finished? Have yra perfect construction dalis ir eina prieš V3.
Common mistakes:
❌ Do you have finished? → ✅ Have you finished?
❌ Did she has a meeting? → ✅ Did she have a meeting?
❌ I have solved the problem = main verb. → Čia have yra auxiliary, solved = V3.
Don't confuse with: Žiūrėk į žodį po have: noun → dažnai main verb; V3 → auxiliary Perfect.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have + noun = main verb.
have/has/had + V3 = Perfect auxiliary.
Do with have tik kai have yra main verb.

Lesson / Topic: Clauses of contrast, purpose, reason and result
Core idea: Jungiančios konstrukcijos parodo, kaip viena idėja susijusi su kita: contrast, purpose, reason arba result.
Main rule / explanation: Contrast: although/even though/whereas/while. Purpose: to/in order to/so that. Reason: because/since/as. Result: so/therefore/as a result/such...that/so...that.
Form / structure: although + clause. to + V1. because + clause. so/therefore + result. such...that / so...that.
When / why we use it: Linking structure rinkis pagal loginį ryšį, o ne pagal vertimą.
Examples:
Although the task was difficult, we completed it. → Nors užduotis buvo sunki, ją atlikome.
We changed the process to reduce errors. → Pakeitėme procesą, kad sumažintume klaidų.
We stayed inside because it was raining. → Likome viduje, nes lijo.
The system was overloaded, so the service became slow. → Sistema buvo perkrauta, todėl paslauga sulėtėjo.
It was so busy that we had to wait. → Buvo taip užimta, kad turėjome laukti.
Special cases / exceptions: Po although/even though reikia clause. Po despite/in spite of – noun arba V-ing. Purpose ir result atsako į skirtingus klausimus.
Common mistakes:
❌ Although it was expensive, but we bought it. → ✅ Although it was expensive, we bought it.
❌ Despite it was expensive... → ✅ Despite the high price... / Despite being expensive...
Don't confuse with: Purpose = kam / kokiu tikslu? Reason = kodėl? Result = kas gavosi? Contrast = kas netikėtai skiriasi?
Quick summary / memory hook:
although/even though = contrast.
to/in order to/so that = purpose.
because/since/as = reason.
so/therefore/as a result = result.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Kai žmogaus lytis nežinoma, nesvarbi arba nenurodyta, šiuolaikinėje standartinėje anglų kalboje dažnai vartojamas singular they.
Main rule / explanation: They/them/their gali reikšti vieną žmogų: someone, every applicant, a customer. Tai padeda nekartoti his or her.
Form / structure: someone/every + noun + they/them/their. Singular they išlaiko nuoseklumą tekste.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai kalbame apie žmogų, kurio gender nenurodytas arba nesvarbus.
Examples:
If a customer has a question, they can contact support. → Jei klientas turi klausimą, jis gali kreiptis į pagalbą.
Someone left their phone here. → Kažkas čia paliko savo telefoną.
Every applicant should check their email. → Kiekvienas kandidatas turėtų patikrinti savo el. paštą.
Special cases / exceptions: Pronoun pasirinkimas turi išlikti consistent viename sakinyje / tekste.
Common mistakes:
❌ Every applicant should check his or her email, then they should reply. → Geriau nuosekliai: Every applicant should check their email, then they should reply.
❌ Someone left her phone here. (jei gender nežinomas) → ✅ Someone left their phone here.
Don't confuse with: Singular they nereiškia, kad būtinai kalbama apie kelis žmones.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Singular they = one person with unknown/irrelevant gender.
they/them/their išlaiko plural pronoun gramatiką, bet gali reikšti vieną žmogų.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Reflexive pronouns grįžta į subject: I hurt myself. Reciprocal pronouns rodo abipusį veiksmą: They helped each other.
Main rule / explanation: Reflexive: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Reciprocal: each other / one another.
Form / structure: subject + verb + reflexive. subject + verb + each other/one another.
When / why we use it: Reflexive – subject ir object yra tas pats žmogus. Reciprocal – du ar daugiau žmonių veikia vienas kitą.
Examples:
I hurt myself. → Aš susižeidžiau.
She introduced herself. → Ji prisistatė.
I did it myself. → Aš pats tai padariau.
They helped each other. → Jie padėjo vienas kitam.
The two teams respect one another. → Abi komandos gerbia viena kitą.
Special cases / exceptions: Reflexive gali būti ir pabrėžimo forma. Nenaudok jo vien dėl to, kad atrodo formaliau.
Common mistakes:
❌ Please contact myself. → ✅ Please contact me.
❌ They looked at themselves. (jei reikšmė „vienas į kitą“) → ✅ They looked at each other.
Don't confuse with: themselves = kiekvienas į save; each other = vienas į kitą.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Reflexive = back to subject.
Reciprocal = one another.
Emphasis: I did it myself.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: There ir it gali užimti subject poziciją, bet įveda skirtingą informaciją. There praneša apie egzistavimą / atsiradimą, it dažnai nurodo situaciją, orą, laiką, atstumą arba veikia kaip preparatory subject.
Main rule / explanation: There introduces existence/occurrence. It refers to a situation, weather, time, distance or can be preparatory subject: It's important to check the data.
Form / structure: There is/are + noun. It + be/adjective/time/weather/etc. It + adjective + to-infinitive.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kad atskirtume egzistavimą / occurrence nuo situacijos vertinimo, oro, laiko, atstumo ar veiksmo.
Examples:
There is a problem with the system. → Sistemoje yra problema.
There are several reasons for the delay. → Yra kelios vėlavimo priežastys.
It's difficult to explain. → Sunku paaiškinti.
It's raining. → Lyja.
It's five o'clock. → Penkta valanda.
It's important to check the data. → Svarbu patikrinti duomenis.
Special cases / exceptions: Nepainiok There is a problem = egzistuoja problema ir It is a problem = tai yra problema. Preparatory it leidžia real subject nukelti vėliau.
Common mistakes:
❌ It is a problem. (jei norime tiesiog pranešti, kad problema egzistuoja) → ✅ There is a problem.
❌ There is difficult to explain. → ✅ It's difficult to explain.
Don't confuse with: Ar kažkas yra? → there. Ar vertiname situaciją / veiksmą / orą / laiką / atstumą? → it.
Quick summary / memory hook:
there = existence/occurrence.
it = situation/weather/time/distance/preparatory subject.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Advanced narrative tenses padeda organizuoti istoriją: pagrindinius įvykius, foną, ankstesnius įvykius, trukmę iki praeities momento, senus įpročius ir pasikartojančius veiksmus.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple = main events. Past Continuous = background. Past Perfect = earlier event. Past Perfect Continuous = duration/activity before a past point. Used to = old habits/states. Would = repeated past actions.
Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing. used to + V1. would + V1 for repeated action.
When / why we use it: Kombinuok formas, kad skaitytojui būtų aiškus timeline ir pasikartojančio veiksmo pobūdis.
Examples:
I opened the email and called the client. → Atidariau laišką ir paskambinau klientui.
I was driving when the message arrived. → Važiavau, kai atėjo žinutė.
They had already left when I arrived. → Kai atvykau, jie jau buvo išėję.
She had been waiting for an hour when the bus came. → Kai atvažiavo autobusas, ji jau buvo laukusi valandą.
I used to live there. → Anksčiau ten gyvenau.
Every summer, we would visit the coast. → Kiekvieną vasarą važiuodavome į pajūrį.
Special cases / exceptions: Would paprastai neapibūdina past states: I used to be shy, ne I would be shy. Past Perfect nereikia automatiškai kiekvienam ankstesniam veiksmui.
Common mistakes:
❌ I would be shy as a child. → ✅ I used to be shy as a child.
❌ She had left before he arrived – to pakanka. Nereikia visų praeities veiksmų daryti Past Perfect.
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia sudaryk timeline, tada rinkis tense. Habits: used to/would.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple = main story.
Past Continuous = background.
Past Perfect = earlier.
Past Perfect Continuous = duration.
used to = past habit/state.
would = repeated past action.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Get yra ypač dažnas veiksmažodis, turintis daug reikšmių. Jo negalima versti vienu lietuvišku žodžiu.
Main rule / explanation: Get + adjective = become. Get + noun = obtain/receive. Get + place = arrive. Get + object + adjective = cause something to become. Get + object + V3 = arrange/cause. Get + -ing = start. Taip pat yra phrasal verbs.
Form / structure: get + adjective/noun/place. get + object + adjective/V3. get + -ing. get + particle.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai get reikšmę lemia visa konstrukcija ir kontekstas.
Examples:
I get tired after work. → Po darbo pavargstu.
I got a message. → Gavau žinutę.
What time did you get home? → Kelintą valandą grįžai namo?
Let's get moving. → Pajudėkime / pradėkime judėti.
Get the report checked. → Organizuok ataskaitos patikrinimą.
Get the room ready. → Paruošk kambarį.
Special cases / exceptions: Context is essential. Get in get up/get through/get along ir kiti phrasal verbs turi savo reikšmes.
Common mistakes:
❌ Mokytis get = tik „gauti“. → Reikia mokytis whole phrase.
❌ get to home → ✅ get home.
Don't confuse with: Žiūrėk, kas eina po get ir ar yra particle. Tai dažnai nulemia meaning.
Quick summary / memory hook:
get + adjective = become.
get + noun = receive/obtain.
get + place = arrive.
get + object + adj/V3 = cause/arrange.
get + -ing = start.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Discourse markers rodo loginį ryšį tarp idėjų ir daro kalbą / tekstą aiškesnį.
Main rule / explanation: Adding: also, moreover, in addition, besides. Contrast: however, nevertheless, on the other hand. Result: therefore, consequently, as a result. Example: for example, for instance. Sequence: first, then, meanwhile, finally. Conclusion: overall, in conclusion.
Form / structure: Marker + clause/sentence, vieta priklauso nuo marker ir stiliaus. Raštu svarbi punctuation.
When / why we use it: Rinkis marker pagal logiką: addition, contrast, result, example, sequence arba conclusion.
Examples:
The plan is expensive. However, it may be effective. → Planas brangus. Tačiau jis gali būti veiksmingas.
Therefore, we changed the schedule. → Todėl pakeitėme tvarkaraštį.
For example, the first option is faster. → Pavyzdžiui, pirmasis variantas greitesnis.
Overall, the results are positive. → Apskritai rezultatai teigiami.
Special cases / exceptions: Kai kurie markers yra formalesni už kitus. However dažnas kalboje ir raštu; moreover gali skambėti formaliau. Ne visi yra tiesioginiai vienas kito vertimai.
Common mistakes:
❌ Naudoti therefore kaip paprastą however sinonimą. → Jie rodo skirtingus loginius ryšius.
❌ The plan is expensive however it may work. → Raštu: The plan is expensive. However, it may work.
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia nustatyk loginį ryšį, tada rinkis marker.
Quick summary / memory hook:
adding → also/moreover.
contrast → however/nevertheless.
result → therefore/as a result.
example → for example.
sequence → first/finally.
conclusion → overall/in conclusion.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Speculation and deduction – modal verbs and expressions
Core idea: Modal verbs ir expressions leidžia parodyti tikrumo laipsnį: strong conclusion, possibility, impossibility arba probability.
Main rule / explanation: Must = strong logical conclusion. Might/may/could = possibility. Can't = strong impossibility. Past deduction: modal + have + V3. Taip pat likely/unlikely/bound to/probably.
Form / structure: must/might/may/could/can't + V1/be. Past: modal + have + V3. likely/unlikely/bound to + V1.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai kalbame ne apie faktą, o apie tai, kiek užtikrintai spėjame.
Examples:
They must be at home. → Jie, turbūt, yra namuose.
They might be at home. → Galbūt jie namuose.
That can't be the right address. → Tai negali būti teisingas adresas.
They must have forgotten. → Turbūt jie pamiršo.
She might have missed the train. → Galbūt ji nespėjo į traukinį.
Special cases / exceptions: Must gali reikšti obligation arba deduction. Kontekstą rodo: You must leave now. / You must have left already.
Common mistakes:
❌ She might has left. → ✅ She might have left.
❌ He must leave = deduction. → Ne, tai obligation; deduction: He must have left.
Don't confuse with: Pirmiausia paklausk: rule/obligation ar evidence-based conclusion?
Quick summary / memory hook:
must = strong deduction.
might/may/could = possibility.
can't = impossible.
Past deduction = modal + have + V3.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Inversion with negative adverbials – adding emphasis
Core idea: Formaliai ir pabrėžiamai vartojamoje anglų kalboje pradinis negative/restrictive adverbial gali sukelti inversion: auxiliary eina prieš subject.
Main rule / explanation: Po Never, Rarely, Seldom, Hardly, Not only, Under no circumstances, At no time ir panašių expressions vartojama inversion. Jei auxiliary nėra, pridedame do/does/did.
Form / structure: Never + auxiliary + subject + verb. Rarely do we... Not only did she...
When / why we use it: Naudojame stipriam emphasis ir formalesniam stiliui.
Examples:
Never had I seen such a result. → Niekada nebuvau matęs tokio rezultato.
Rarely do we see such results. → Retai matome tokius rezultatus.
Not only did she solve the problem, but she also explained it clearly. → Ji ne tik išsprendė problemą, bet ir aiškiai ją paaiškino.
Special cases / exceptions: Tai formal/emphatic structure, o ne įprasta šnekamosios kalbos tvarka.
Common mistakes:
❌ Never I have seen... → ✅ Never have I seen...
❌ Rarely we see... → ✅ Rarely do we see...
Don't confuse with: Pradinis negative/restrictive expression → patikrink, ar reikia inversion.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Never/Rarely/Seldom + auxiliary + subject.
No auxiliary? → use do/does/did.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Distancing – expressions and passive of reporting verbs
Core idea: Distancing leidžia pateikti informaciją taip, kad jos nevaizduotume kaip asmeniškai patikrinto fakto.
Main rule / explanation: Vartojami It is said/believed, It appears/seems, According to, Apparently ir passive reporting. Šios formos ypač būdingos journalism, academic writing ir professional reports.
Form / structure: It is said that... / It appears that... / The company is believed to... / According to... / Apparently,...
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai yra informacijos šaltinis, bet kalbėtojas nori atsiriboti nuo teiginio.
Examples:
It is believed that the company will expand. → Manoma, kad įmonė plėsis.
The company is believed to be expanding. → Manoma, kad įmonė plečiasi.
He is thought to have left. → Manoma, kad jis išėjo.
Apparently, the figures are incorrect. → Atrodo, kad skaičiai neteisingi.
Special cases / exceptions: Distancing neturi sukurti klaidingo certainty įspūdžio. Formuluotė turi atspindėti available evidence.
Common mistakes:
❌ It is definitely believed... be pagrindo. → Distancing tikslas – parodyti source/uncertainty.
❌ He is thought has left. → ✅ He is thought to have left.
Don't confuse with: Distancing = „perduodu šaltinį / informaciją, bet nepateikiu jos kaip savo tiesioginio fakto“.
Quick summary / memory hook:
It is said/believed...
It appears/seems...
According to...
Apparently...
The company is believed to...
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Wish, rather, if only, it's time – Unreal uses of past tenses
Core idea: Wish, if only, would rather ir it's time naudoja past forms, kad parodytų nerealumą, apgailestavimą arba tai, kad dabar jau metas keisti situaciją.
Main rule / explanation: Present unreal: wish/if only + Past Simple. Past regret: + Past Perfect. Would rather apie kito žmogaus veiksmą + Past Simple. It's time + Past Simple gali reikšti dabartį / artimą ateitį.
Form / structure: wish + V2. wish + had + V3. would rather + person + Past Simple. it's time + Past Simple.
When / why we use it: Naudojame, kai išreiškiame unreal present, regret about past, preference about another person arba tai, kad dabar jau metas veikti.
Examples:
I wish I knew the answer. → Norėčiau žinoti atsakymą.
If only I had more time. → Jei tik turėčiau daugiau laiko.
I wish I had prepared better. → Gaila, kad geriau nepasiruošiau.
I'd rather you didn't tell them yet. → Verčiau norėčiau, kad dar jiems nesakytum.
It's time we left. → Mums jau metas išeiti.
Special cases / exceptions: Past form čia nebūtinai reiškia past time. Ji rodo distance from reality.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish I know the answer. → ✅ I wish I knew the answer.
❌ It's time we leave. → ✅ It's time we left.
Don't confuse with: Neversti Past form tiesiog kaip praeities. Žiūrėk į funkciją: unreal, regret, preference, urgency.
Quick summary / memory hook:
wish + Past = unreal present.
wish + Past Perfect = past regret.
would rather + person + Past.
It's time + Past.
QA / notes: Translated from the RU master; English formulas and English example source text preserved.

Core idea: Kai kurie veiksmažodžiai su objektu reikalauja infinitivo arba -ing formos; pasirinkimas priklauso nuo veiksmažodžio.
Main rule / explanation: want/expect/allow/encourage + object + to V1; catch/find/keep + object + V-ing; make/let + object + bendratis be to. remember gali keisti reikšmę.
Form / structure: verb + object + to V1; verb + object + V-ing; make/let + object + V1.
When / why we use it: Mokykis visą derinį veiksmažodis + objektas + kita forma, o ne vien atskirą veiksmažodį.
Examples:
The manager encouraged us to apply. → Vadovas paskatino mus pateikti paraišką.
I found him working late. → Radau jį dirbantį iki vėlumos.
The manager made us wait. → Vadovas privertė mus laukti.
They let us leave early. → Jie leido mums išeiti anksčiau.
I remember meeting her. → Prisimenu, kaip su ja susipažinau.
I remembered to call her. → Nepamiršau jai paskambinti.
Special cases / exceptions: remember + -ing reiškia prisiminimą apie praeities įvykį; remember + to V1 – prisiminti, kad reikia atlikti veiksmą. Po make/let vartojama bendratis be to.
Common mistakes:
❌ She encouraged me apply. → ✅ She encouraged me to apply.
❌ They made us to wait. → ✅ They made us wait.
❌ I remember to meeting her. → ✅ I remember meeting her.
Don't confuse with: Žiūrėk ne tik į pirmą veiksmažodį, bet ir į jo valdomą objektą bei tolesnę konstrukciją.
Quick summary / memory hook: Mokykis kaip vienetą: verb + object + reikiama forma.
QA / notes: Išversta iš RU master; angliškos formulės ir angliško pavyzdžio dalis prieš → išsaugotos.

Lesson / Topic: Unless, even if, provided, as long as, etc. – Other expressions in conditionals
Core idea: Unless, even if, provided ir as long as išreiškia skirtingas sąlygas.
Main rule / explanation: Unless = if not; even if rodo, kad rezultatas nesikeis; provided/providing/as long as nurodo sąlygą, kuri turi būti įvykdyta.
Form / structure: unless + Present; even if + Present; provided/providing/as long as + clause.
When / why we use it: Naudok šias konstrukcijas, kai reikia tiksliai parodyti sąlygos tipą. Ateities šalutiniame sakinyje po jų paprastai nevartojame will.
Examples:
Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train. → Jei neskubėsi, pavėluosi į traukinį.
Even if it rains, we'll go. → Net jei lis, mes eisime.
You can borrow it provided that you return it tomorrow. → Gali tai pasiskolinti, jei tik rytoj grąžinsi.
You can stay as long as you keep the room clean. → Gali pasilikti, jei tik palaikysi kambarį švarų.
Special cases / exceptions: Po unless, even if ir kitų sąlyginių junginių, kalbant apie ateitį, vartojamas Present: unless it rains, ne unless it will rain.
Common mistakes:
❌ Unless it will rain, we'll go. → ✅ Unless it rains, we'll go.
❌ Even if it will be difficult, we'll continue. → ✅ Even if it is difficult, we'll continue.
Don't confuse with: unless nėra tas pats, kas paprastas if; even if pabrėžia, kad sąlyga rezultato nepakeis.
Quick summary / memory hook: unless = if not; even if = net jei; provided/as long as = jei tik.

Lesson / Topic: All conditionals – mixed conditionals, alternatives to if, inversion
Core idea: Visos Conditional struktūros turi skirtingą ryšį tarp laiko ir realybės; ši tema apima Mixed Conditional, alternatyvas if ir formalią inversiją.
Main rule / explanation: Galime vartoti unless/provided/as long as/on condition that/supposing/assuming. Formalioje kalboje galimos inversijos: Had I known..., Were I..., Should you...
Form / structure: Mixed: If + past perfect, would + present/base. Arba If + past, would have + V3. Inversion: Had/Were/Should + subject...
When / why we use it: Naudok, kai sąlygos laikas ir rezultato laikas skiriasi arba kai norima formalesnės konstrukcijos.
Examples:
If I had studied engineering, I would have a different job now. → Jei būčiau studijavęs inžineriją, dabar turėčiau kitą darbą.
If I weren't so busy, I would have joined you yesterday. → Jei nebūčiau toks užsiėmęs, vakar būčiau prisijungęs prie jūsų.
Had I known, I would have acted differently. → Jei būčiau žinojęs, būčiau pasielgęs kitaip.
Were I in your position, I would wait. → Jei būčiau tavo vietoje, palaukčiau.
Should you need assistance, contact support. → Jei jums prireiktų pagalbos, kreipkitės į pagalbos tarnybą.
Special cases / exceptions: Inversija nekeičia pagrindinės reikšmės, bet suteikia formalesnį toną. Po Had/Were/Should neįterpk papildomo if.
Common mistakes:
❌ Had I knew... → ✅ Had I known...
❌ Were I was in your position... → ✅ Were I in your position...
❌ Should you will need assistance... → ✅ Should you need assistance...
Don't confuse with: Tai ne vien įprastas first/second/third conditional: laiko ryšys gali būti mišrus.
Quick summary / memory hook: Mixed = skirtingi laikai vienoje sąlygoje; Had/Were/Should = formali inversija.
QA / notes: Išversta iš RU master; angliškos formulės ir angliško pavyzdžio dalis prieš → išsaugotos.

Core idea: Mixed conditionals sieja praeities sąlygą su dabarties rezultatu arba dabarties sąlygą su praeities rezultatu.
Main rule / explanation: Past Perfect sąlygos dalyje parodo praeities priežastį, o would + V1 – dabarties rezultatą. Present condition su would have + V3 kalba apie praeities rezultatą.
Form / structure: Past→present: If + had + V3, would + V1. Present→past: If + V2, would have + V3.
When / why we use it: Naudok, kai vienos dalies laikas ir kitos dalies laikas nesutampa.
Examples:
If I had taken that job, I would live abroad now. → Jei būčiau priėmęs tą darbą, dabar gyvenčiau užsienyje.
If I were more organised, I wouldn't have missed the deadline yesterday. → Jei būčiau labiau organizuotas, vakar nebūčiau praleidęs termino.
Special cases / exceptions: Pirmiausia nustatyk, ar kalbi apie praeities priežastį su dabarties rezultatu, ar apie dabartinę būseną, kuri paveiktų praeitį.
Common mistakes:
❌ If I had taken that job, I would have live abroad now. → ✅ ... I would live abroad now.
❌ If I were organised, I wouldn't miss the deadline yesterday. → ✅ ... I wouldn't have missed the deadline yesterday.
Don't confuse with: Nesupainiok su trečiuoju sąlyginiu, kuriame ir sąlyga, ir rezultatas yra praeityje.
Quick summary / memory hook: Past → now arba now → past = mixed conditional.

Lesson / Topic: Modal verbs – permission, obligation, prohibition, necessity
Core idea: Modal verbs tiksliai parodo pareigą, draudimą, būtinybės nebuvimą ir leidimą.
Main rule / explanation: must = stipri pareiga; have to = išorinė taisyklė; mustn't = draudimas; don't have to/needn't = nebūtina; can/may = leidimas; be allowed to tinka įvairiems laikams.
Form / structure: must/have to/mustn't/don't have to/needn't + V1; can/may + V1; be allowed to + V1.
When / why we use it: Rinkis formą pagal tai, ar kažkas privaloma, draudžiama, nebūtina ar leidžiama.
Examples:
You must wear a badge. → Turite nešioti ženklelį.
We have to submit the form by Friday. → Turime pateikti formą iki penktadienio.
You mustn't share this password. → Negalite dalytis šiuo slaptažodžiu.
You don't have to attend. → Jums nebūtina dalyvauti.
You may leave early. → Galite išeiti anksčiau.
We weren't allowed to enter. → Mums nebuvo leista įeiti.
Special cases / exceptions: mustn't reiškia draudimą, o don't have to/needn't – tik būtinybės nebuvimą.
Common mistakes:
❌ You mustn't attend = „nebūtina dalyvauti“. → Tai reiškia „draudžiama dalyvauti“.
✅ You don't have to attend. = dalyvauti nebūtina.
Don't confuse with: Draudimas nėra tas pats, kas nebūtina; leidimas nėra tas pats, kas pareiga.
Quick summary / memory hook: must = privalai; mustn't = negalima; don't have to = nebūtina; may/can = galima.
QA / notes: Išversta iš RU master; angliškos formulės ir angliško pavyzdžio dalis prieš → išsaugotos.

Core idea: Jutimo veiksmažodžiai aprašo pojūtį ir tai, ką matome, girdime ar jaučiame.
Main rule / explanation: Jutimo Verb konstrukcijos: look/sound/smell/taste/feel + adjective; verb + like + noun; see/hear/watch/notice/feel + Object + V1/V-ing.
Form / structure: look/sound/smell/taste/feel + adjective; verb + like + noun; see/hear/watch/notice/feel + object + V1/V-ing.
When / why we use it: Naudok, kai aprašai jutiminį įspūdį arba stebi kitą veiksmą.
Examples:
The plan sounds reasonable. → Planas skamba pagrįstai.
It looks like a mistake. → Atrodo, kad tai klaida.
I saw him cross the street. → Mačiau, kaip jis perėjo gatvę.
I saw him crossing the street. → Mačiau jį einantį per gatvę.
The soup tastes good. → Sriuba skani.
Special cases / exceptions: Su jutimo veiksmažodžiais po feel/taste/smell dažnai vartojamas būdvardis. Po see/hear galima V1 arba V-ing, priklausomai nuo reikšmės.
Common mistakes:
❌ The soup tastes well. → ✅ The soup tastes good.
❌ I saw him to cross the street. → ✅ I saw him cross the street.
Don't confuse with: V1 po see/hear dažnai apima visą veiksmą; V-ing pabrėžia tuo metu vykusį veiksmą.
Quick summary / memory hook: Sense verb + adjective; see/hear + object + V1/V-ing.
